items.title: Fears over interest rate rise and jobs send UK consumer confidence to three-year low
items.summary: Blow to John Healey before budget as UK households face ‘notable strain’ on their finances Business live – latest updates Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey. In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”. Continue reading...
items.body:
Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey.
In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”.
The chancellor could announce tax rises in his first budget to offset the rising cost of government borrowing, which has soared in response to the conflict in the Middle East.
S&P Global said consumers were concerned about the likelihood of an increase in interest rates by the Bank of England. More than 50% of 1,500 respondents said they expected a rise in the cost of borrowing over the next year.
Fixed-rate mortgage costs have already jumped to multi-year highs in the UK, while the threat of artificial intelligence and caution among employers about hiring new staff sent consumer confidence in the jobs market plunging to its lowest level in three-and-a-half years.
The average two-year fixed residential mortgage rate rose to 5.88% on Monday, its highest since 16 April and up from 5.84% last Friday, while the average five-year is at its highest since October 2023, at 5.92%, up from 5.88%, data from Moneyfacts showed.
The rise in mortgage costs is expected to add about £150 to monthly mortgage payments, based on a typical loan of £250,000 over 25 years, since the start of March 2026.
Official figures have shown that the average direct debit to cover monthly mortgage costs has risen over the past four years from about £600 to £900.
Maryam Baluch, an economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said a downbeat mood was spreading across UK households “as improved sentiment surrounding the new government is eroded by renewed worries over energy prices, the cost of living and job prospects”.
She said: “Against a backdrop of rising volatility in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East, households increasingly reported difficulties accessing credit, suggesting that expectations of tighter monetary conditions are beginning to feed through to borrowing conditions. Together, these factors point to cautiousness about both financial prospects and pose some downside risks to the broader economic outlook.”
Analysts believe the jobs market has proved resilient since the US attack on Iran and a steep rise in the cost of fuel and energy, but a steady decline in the number of payrolled employees over the past six months and a drop in vacancies to a five-year low have shown employers are worried about their profitability over the next year.
The British Chamber of Commerce has called for the government to give businesses extra support after a series of tax rises over the past two years, including an increase in employers national insurance payments.
A survey by the business organisation of 5,000 companies in the second quarter of 2026 found that only 17% were planning to increase investment in the coming months, a post-pandemic low.
Last week, Andy Burnham said he will need to take “difficult decisions” on the economy to ensure that it “remains on track”.
In response to the growing clamour for tax cuts to support businesses and households hit by the cost of living crisis, the Liberal Democrat leader, Ed Davey, said at his party conference that the UK should cut fuel duty to offset some of the rise in petrol and diesel prices at the pumps.
The German government on Monday announced plans for a cut in tax on fuel of about 15p to take effect on 1 October.
Healey could limit his tax rises to wealthier groups, including a rise in capital gains tax. However, analysts say he is unlikely to raise sufficient funds from discreet tax rises to pay for higher defence spending and the rise in debt costs while preserving a reserve buffer, often referred to as headroom, of at least £20bn.

items.title: PepsiCo unveils Christmas 2026 savoury snacking line-up
items.summary: PepsiCo is helping retailers get their savoury snacking aisles festive-ready with a seasonal line up of reskins, alongside four bold limited-edition launches. With Christmas packs landing on shelves from 28 September across Walkers, Doritos, Sensations and Wotsits Giants, PepsiCo’s seasonal activity brings together familiar favourites… This story continues at PepsiCo unveils Christmas 2026 savoury snacking line-up Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
With Christmas packs landing on shelves from 28 September across Walkers, Doritos, Sensations and Wotsits Giants, PepsiCo’s seasonal activity brings together familiar favourites and festive flavours.
Fan favourites remain key for Walkers, Doritos and Sensations during Christmas, with core flavours having accounted for more than 95% of total crisp sales in 2025, according to Nielsen IQ data.
Designed with clear Christmas cues, such as Christmas trees, stars and festive baubles, the reskins bring a festive twist to some of PepsiCo’s biggest core snacks.
Pepsico said this will help popular SKUs stand out on shelf, giving retailers a strong seasonal offering to compliment the new flavour launches.
The limited-edition range includes Doritos Gingerbread, back for a second year after generating more than one million organic TikTok views last Christmas.
Sensations Honey Glazed Roast Ham also returns, building on an 82% repurchase intent in 2025. Also making a comeback are Walkers Pigs in Blankets and Roast Potatoes multipacks, which last appeared in 2023 and 2021 respectively, both with new non-HFSS recipes for 2026.
These innovations tap into shoppers’ appetite for something different at Christmas.
Rob Pothier, marketing director at PepsiCo, said: “Christmas is a huge opportunity for savoury snacking, with shoppers stocking up for every occasion, from family get-togethers and parties to nights in and the days between Christmas and New Year.
“In fact, 84% of shoppers say they stock up on snacks before the festivities begin [according to a Toluna poll], so retailers will want to make sure they have a strong mix of core favourites and seasonal flavours to give shoppers plenty of choice throughout the festive period.
“Our Christmas portfolio is designed to stand out in store and make it easy for shoppers to find what they need, whether that’s a familiar favourite or a seasonal flavour.”
The range will be supported by shopper marketing activity to drive visibility throughout the festive period.

items.title: Joe Marler and Tony Bellew challenge what it means to ‘man up’ in Jacamo’s AW26 campaign, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. N Brown Group, the inclusive fashion and retail platform, today unveils the latest Autumn/Winter campaign from its leading menswear brand Jacamo, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’, starring former England rugby international and Jacamo brand ambassador Joe Marler, alongside former professional boxer Tony Bellew. The campaign marks the next phase of Jacamo’s partnership with Marler following his appointment […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
N Brown Group, the inclusive fashion and retail platform, today unveils the latest Autumn/Winter campaign from its leading menswear brand Jacamo, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’, starring former England rugby international and Jacamo brand ambassador Joe Marler, alongside former professional boxer Tony Bellew.
The campaign marks the next phase of Jacamo’s partnership with Marler following his appointment as brand ambassador earlier this year. For Autumn/Winter, he is joined by Bellew as the pair head into the great outdoors to take on an epic challenge and a series of missions – including abseiling, kayaking, and reservoir jumping – all inspired by nature and the four elements.
Combining Joe and Tony’s competitive personalities and humour with Jacamo’s Autumn/Winter collection, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’ puts both the men and their clothing to the test. The pair take on a series of challenges that see them confront the elements as well as their own personal fears. Marler, who cannot swim, is challenged to jump from a rock face into a deep reservoir, while Bellew, who is afraid of heights, takes on an abseil down a cliff face.
Beyond the physical challenges, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’ also explores the pressures facing men today and what it means to show strength. New research commissioned by Jacamo found that 40% of men find it easier to face a physical fear than admit an emotional struggle.
The research, conducted among 2,000 men aged 25 to 55, also found that 94% have experienced what they describe as a “dark period” in life – a time when they felt overwhelmed, lost, isolated or were struggling beneath the surface. Among those, almost a third (31%) said nobody knew how much they were really struggling.
Reflecting these findings, Joe and Tony open up throughout the campaign about attitudes towards masculinity and the expectation to “man up”, as well as work and financial pressures, loneliness, checking in with friends and family, and the importance of opening up when things become difficult.
A 10-minute film is available on the dedicated Jacamo campaign page and Jacamo’s YouTube channel. The campaign is also running across Jacamo’s social channels, and Sky and ITVX, directing viewers to watch the full film on Jacamo.
As part of the campaign, Jacamo is partnering with men’s suicide prevention charity Andy’s Man Club, which provides free, volunteer-led peer-to-peer support groups for men across the UK. From campaign launch until 31 December, Jacamo will donate £1 to Andy’s Man Club for every Jacamo branded sweatshirt, hoodie or jogger sold, supporting the charity’s work to challenge the stigma surrounding men’s mental health and encourage more men to talk.
Esme Stone, head of brand at N Brown, said: “Following the fantastic response to our partnership with Joe, we wanted to build on that momentum for Autumn/Winter with a campaign that feels unmistakably Jacamo: entertaining, authentic and rooted in the things that matter to our customers.
“We wanted this campaign to play with the idea of strength – both physical and emotional. The research shows that many men still struggle to talk about what they’re going through, and why creating space for those conversations matters. ‘Jacamo vs Nature’ gives us a brilliant opportunity to showcase our Autumn/Winter collection, while Joe and Tony’s natural chemistry brings the campaign to life. Both are known for their physical strength, competitiveness and humour, but what makes this campaign powerful is their willingness to talk openly about the pressures men face. Seeing two men so closely associated with traditional masculinity embrace vulnerability is incredibly important, and we hope it encourages other men to do the same.
“Our partnership with Andy’s Man Club builds on those conversations, helping encourage more men to check in with their mates and talk openly.”
Joe Marler, Jacamo brand ambassador, said: “I’ve really enjoyed working with Jacamo as a brand ambassador, so it’s been great to get stuck into another campaign with them – especially one that involved working alongside Tony. We’re both very competitive, so there was plenty of messing about, but we also had some proper, honest conversations along the way. Men aren’t always great at saying how they’re really doing, so if this campaign encourages a few more people to check in with their mates, that’s a good thing.”
Tony Bellew, former professional boxer and pundit, said: “I’m always up for a challenge, so when Jacamo asked me to work alongside Joe to take on some outdoors challenges, I couldn’t say no. We had a lot of fun taking on the elements and putting the gear through its paces, but what I enjoyed most were the conversations we had along the way.
“There’s still a lot of pressure on men to be tough, keep things to themselves and just get on with it. Sometimes the strongest thing you can do is talk to someone and let them know how you’re really doing. If this campaign gets a few more lads checking in on their mates, then that can only be a good thing.”
Luke Ambler, head of partnerships at Andy’s Man Club, said: “We’re thrilled to partner with Jacamo on a campaign that helps bring conversations around men’s mental health into the everyday. When men who are used to talking about strength and performance are prepared to talk openly about how they’re really doing, it can help challenge the idea that vulnerability is weakness. Through this partnership, we hope to encourage more men to check in with each other, open up and know that support is there when they need it.”

items.title: JD Sports launches in Mexico amid North American slowdown
items.summary: JD Sports has announced plans to open more than 140 shops in Mexico, as the ‘King of Trainers’ battles to halt falling sales and move on from a recent boardroom bust-up. The FTSE 100 retailer said it has reached an agreement with Axo, a Mexico-based retail distributor, to operate its stores in the country.  JD [...]
items.body:
JD Sports launches in Mexico amid North American slowdown
JD Sports has announced plans to open more than 140 shops in Mexico, as the ‘King of Trainers’ battles to halt falling sales and move on from a recent boardroom bust-up.
The FTSE 100 retailer said it has reached an agreement with Axo, a Mexico-based retail distributor, to operate its stores in the country.
JD Sports will hope that this expansion halts the sales slowdown it is seeing in its crucial North American market. The region currently accounts for 38 per cent of its global turnover but sales here fell by 6.8 per cent in the three months to August.
Under the deal, Axo will operate JD’s stores and online retail using its brand and intellectual property, with the shoe and sportswear seller set to offer a “differentiated proposition” to the Mexican market.
The FTSE 100 retailer believes there is huge potential in the Mexican market, telling shareholders that about 40 per cent of its 130m citizens are younger than 25.
“Mexico is a market with a large, highly engaged consumer base and a demographic profile which aligns strongly with JD’s unique position as a curator of footwear and apparel trends across sport, music and fashion,” the group said.
The country’s activewear market is valued at about $6.5bn and is tipped to grow to $10bn by 2034, according to JD.
Régis Schultz, JD’s chief executive, said: “JD’s product offering aligns closely with consumer demand in Mexico and we believe our position at the intersection of sport, music and fashion will deepen the connection we have with that consumer.”
Schultz added that Axo’s “deep market expertise, strong operational platform and proven experience with leading international brands make it uniquely placed to help deliver the JD proposition in Mexico and unlock the opportunity that exists there”.
Schultz under pressure
The retailer will begin opening its more-than 140 Mexican stores next year. The group will later upgrade its best-performing sites, in line with its “bigger and better” flagship store strategy.
JD’s deal with Axo marks the latest expansion of its global franchise platform. Between JD and Courir, the French trainer seller it bought in 2024, the group operates 75 franchise stores in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
The ‘King of Trainers’ is launching in Mexico in a rocky period for the group, coming off the back of a profit warning and a boardroom succession row.
Last month, JD slashed its upper profit target by £50m to £800m as it warned that sluggish US sales and intense discounting by its rivals is threatening its growth.
“The market stayed highly promotional, reflecting the consumer and footwear product cycle headwinds our industry has faced in recent quarters, whilst our core consumer was impacted by incremental cost-of-living pressures,” Schultz said.
The retailer’s chief executive has only recently survived a plot to push him out of the company. Earlier this year, JD chairman Andy Higginson quit the group’s board after failing to convince it to oust Schultz.
Investors are growing impatient to see solid signs of progress from Schultz’s growth plan. In August, JD appointed former Ikea boss Peter Agnefjäll to succeed Higginson.

items.title: Demand for hair treatment soars to combat side effects of fat jabs
items.summary: Growing demand for weight-loss drugs has boosted sales of hair products, according to Superdrug and Boots.
items.body:
Demand for hair treatment soars to combat side effects of fat jabs
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Growing demand for weight-loss drugs has boosted sales of hair products, according to Superdrug and Boots.
The drugs - sold under brand names Mounjaro and Wegovy in the UK - are taken as a weekly injection and trick the body into thinking it is full.
But users can suffer from hair thinning or hair loss and are now seeking help.
Online doctor appointments for hair loss have grown 14.9 per cent over the past year while sales of medicated hair care are up 28.8 per cent over two years, according to Superdrug.
The chemist also said that hair treatments have risen 27.7 per cent since 2024, coinciding with an increase in fat jab usage.
Around 6 per cent of households now have at least one user of the appetite-suppressing drugs, compared to 2.3 per cent in 2024, according to researchers at Worldpanel by Numerator. Some 1.9million Britons are thought to be using the jabs.
Shoppers are increasingly looking for products that claim to keep their hair healthy - including tackling side effects of weight-loss drugs.
Chelsey Saunders, director of haircare, skincare and fragrance at Boots, said: ‘As conversations around GLP-1 medications continue to grow, we’re also seeing an increased interest in hair and scalp health, reflected in the types of products customers are seeking within the haircare category.’
Hair products with helpful amino acids - such as keratin and collagen - are flying off the shelves as customers are ‘increasingly ingredient-led’, Saunders added. This is similar to a trend for skincare, she said.
‘Concerns around thinning hair, shedding and density have pushed customers to seek out targeted solutions,’ she said. ‘As a result, demand for efficacy-led products is accelerating.’
Boots is also seeing more shoppers seeking products or routines they have discovered on social media.
Influencer and hair expert Abbey Yung - who is known for sharing an elaborate 11-step routine to her 3.1million followers - has caused certain products, such as a £21 ‘anti-hair loss scalp serum’ from Pantene, to do well.
Saunders added: ‘We’re seeing trichologists, dermatologists and pharmacists becoming the new influencers, and their impact is very real.’

items.title: The return of VAT-free shopping will boost Britain’s towns and cities
items.summary: Britain has so much to offer. It is no surprise that more than forty million overseas visitors choose to visit our country every year. Walk down Bond Street in London or Princes Street in Edinburgh and you will see visitors from around the world drawn to some of our most iconic retailers. Our high streets [...]
items.body:
The return of VAT-free shopping will boost Britain’s towns and cities
Britain has so much to offer. It is no surprise that more than forty million overseas visitors choose to visit our country every year.
Walk down Bond Street in London or Princes Street in Edinburgh and you will see visitors from around the world drawn to some of our most iconic retailers. Our high streets showcase the very best of British design and craftsmanship – from Barbour jackets and Savile Row suits to Mulberry handbags.
But too many tourists are choosing to shop in rival cities outside the UK. Whilst visitor numbers have recovered to near pre-Covid levels, spending remains 8 per cent lower in real terms than before the pandemic. For many high-spending US visitors, the UK is now either a ‘flyover state’ on their way to continental Europe or a cultural stop while the serious shopping takes place elsewhere.
Why would you come to Britain when you can visit Milan or Paris and shop for less? When the UK abolished tax-free shopping in 2021, it left us at a disadvantage compared with other major European destinations. According to VisitBritain, real-terms visitor spending is now lower than before its abolition.
Britain is competing with other countries
The next Conservative government is serious about growing the economy. That means being determined to compete and allowing our brilliant British retailers, hotels, restaurants and attractions to put their best foot forward.
That is why we have announced today that the next Conservative government will restore VAT refunds for eligible visitors. It would be a major boost to British business, so it is no surprise that leading figures are backing our plans, including hotel entrepreneur Sir Rocco Forte, Fortnum & Mason’s Tom Athron and top chef Angela Hartnett OBE.
Independent research conducted by Cebr has found that fully restoring tax-free shopping could attract up to 2.35 million additional visitors and generate £4.1 billion in extra spending. For every £1 of VAT refunded to tourists, an additional £1.56 could be generated in other taxes. We’ll start with the previous scheme, which covered visitors from outside the EU, and then extend it once the net economic benefit has been demonstrated through detailed, data-based evaluations conducted by the Treasury.
Hospitality and retail need a boost
This follows our announcement that we will scrap stamp duty on purchases of a primary home to get the housing market moving again, as well as our plan to relieve hundreds of thousands of high street shops of the burden of business rates. Because so many of us in the Shadow Cabinet have experience in business, we know that cutting taxes, reducing red tape and lower energy costs will help firms succeed and our economy grow, providing much-needed jobs for the next generation.
The contrast with this government couldn’t be clearer. Since Labour came to power, they have hammered our retail and hospitality sectors. They have raised employer National Insurance contributions, hiked business rates, and they now even plan to tax tourism.
Winning is about showing up with a determination to compete. We Conservatives understand that and are ready to support British businesses. That mindset for Britain is what today’s announcement is all about.
Andrew Griffith MP is the Conservative Shadow Chancellor

items.body:
Tally creator Simbe lays claim to largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology
Simbe reports that it has surpassed 3,000 autonomous units under contract, which is pitched as the largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology (as identified in the company's research).
In the decade since introducing Tally, an inventory robot, Simbe has been shifting from autonomous shelf digitisation to building a broader platform for the physical store.
Today, Simbe combines autonomous robots, computer vision, RFID, handheld and fixed sensing to continuously capture what is happening inside retail locations: from inventory availability and product location to prices, promotions, and merchandising conditions.
“Retailers are increasingly deploying physical intelligence across the enterprise,” says Deborah Weinswig, Founder and CEO at Coresight Research. “Simbe’s 3,000 unit milestone reflects that shift: trusted shelf-level data is becoming foundational to store operations, digital commerce, merchandising and supply chain decisions.”
Highlights include: More than 75 retail banners globally, including BJ’s Wholesale Club, Kroger, and SPAR; The first and only company to earn UL 3300 certification for a robot designed to operate in public; More than 90% of store managers working alongside Tally say the technology makes their jobs better.
“What works once in a lab doesn’t often work in the real world, and it’s brutally hard to build robotics that operate reliably across thousands of stores for the world’s largest retailers,” says Aidan Madigan-Curtis, General Partner at Eclipse Ventures. “Simbe is the real deal. In a category full of promise, they’re one of the rare companies delivering at global scale, showing how physical AI is becoming essential infrastructure for retail.”
“Retail is one of the clearest proving grounds for physical AI at commercial scale, and this is just the beginning” says Brad Bogolea, Co-founder and CEO at Simbe. “A decade of operating autonomously in stores has given us the foundation to think far beyond the robot. We’re building the physical intelligence layer that enables retailers to understand and operate stores with greater autonomy.”
So hot right now
Simbe is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

items.body:
Equestrian brand LeMieux takes wraps off peer-to-peer resale platform within its mobile app
LeMieux has launched ReRide, a new peer-to-peer resale platform launching exclusively within the retailer's Insiders app, designed to bring its community together while giving quality products a longer life.
A spokesperson says: "By keeping well made products in use for longer, we’re helping reduce waste, encourage more conscious purchasing and create a marketplace where great kit continues its journey with another rider. ReRide is also a destination for collectors and long time LeMieux fans. Whether you’re searching for a discontinued colour, replacing a well loved favourite or completing a matching set from a previous season, ReRide makes it easier to discover those harder to find pieces that are no longer available to buy new."
They add: "Most importantly, ReRide has been created for the LeMieux community. It’s a place where riders can connect directly with one another, share trusted products and help fellow equestrians enjoy the quality and performance of LeMieux for years to come."
Mobile first
Last year, LeMieux announced the launch of its first ever mobile app, combining a points-based rewards programme, an interactive community hub, and what was pitched as a first of its kind equestrian events calendar.
Members can earn rosettes by completing challenges within the app’s community platform - unlocking exclusive rewards, earn coins, and level ups as they go. These points give users access to members only benefits, limited edition products and collaborations, invitations to exclusive Q&A sessions with top riders and influencers, and the chance to join product testing panels and give feedback on future design.
The community platform, meanwhile, offers chatrooms where equestrians can share their passion for horses, seek advice, and support one another. Users can also explore a shoppable gallery of tagged LeMieux looks for outfit inspiration, featuring real riders and friends of the brand from around the world.
Riders in the UK and US can enter a date and location to instantly discover local competitions and events near them.
“We’ve always known how strong and vibrant our community is. This app is our way of bringing everyone together - to listen to them, and to give them a place where they can truly be part of the brand,” says Dan Mahoney, CEO at LeMieux.
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards

Ranju Das talks leading technology and AI strategy for lululemon as he prepares for next adventure
Last month, we reported that Ranju Das was leaving lululemon, where he served as Chief AI and Technology Officer. He joined the retailer in September of last year, with a focus on leveraging AI and technology to redefine the retail landscape, enhancing guest experiences and internal operations.
“Ranju Das has left lululemon. We are grateful for his contributions and wish him well in his next chapter,” a lululemon spokesperson told RTIH “We are conducting a global search for our next technology leader and have full confidence in our current technology teams to continue delivering on our priorities.”
Das has now taken to social media to reflect on his short run with the retailer.

Mamas & Papas keeps it in the family as Chris Greenwood retires and Chris Platt becomes new CIO
It's the end of an era at Mamas & Papas with Chris Greenwood stepping down from the role of CIO and entering the world of retirement. Chris Platt, who joined the retailer in July as IT and Transformation Director, will be taking over from him.
In a LinkedIn post, Greenwood said: "A significant moment for me this week as I formally handed over the leadership of the IT team at Mamas & Papas to Chris Platt after 36 years at the helm. I always thought that handing over after so many years might be difficult. But it becomes much easier when you know you have found the right person."
He added: "Chris has exactly the qualities the role needs. He is calm, thoughtful and approachable, with the experience and judgement to lead the team confidently. He understands that technology is ultimately about enabling people and supporting the wider business and that, at Mamas & Papas, everything we do should reflect the values of a very special brand."
"Just as importantly, he has taken the time to listen, understand the team and appreciate what has already been built. I know he will bring his own ideas and leadership style while continuing to develop the people around him."
Greenwood will remain at Mamas & Papas for the next six months in a consultative capacity, supporting Platt and the wider business through the transition.
He concluded: "Not many people have the opportunity to help choose their own successor, and I feel very fortunate to have done so. I genuinely believe that both the team and the business are in excellent hands, and I wish Chris every success in the role."

London calling
Pop Mart, which is known for selling collectable vinyl figures in mystery blind boxes, recently took to social media to announce the closure of its store in Soho, London.
In an Instagram post, it said: “To our amazing Soho community, thank you for all the wonderful memories, support, and love you’ve shared with us over the years! Our Soho store’s last trading day will be Saturday, 29th August. While we’re saying goodbye to this location, the fun doesn't stop here! You can still find all your favourite Pop Mart collectibles just around the corner at our nearby store: Charing Cross, 69-71 Charing Cross Road, London, WC2H 0NE.”
It did not give a reason for this move, but it is likely that, with the recent opening at Charing Cross Road, alongside a location on nearby Oxford Street, Soho was surplus to requirements.
The Charing Cross location opened in April and is Pop Mart’s largest London store to date. It spans 5,090 square feet and introduces a mezzanine level, a first for one of its stores in the UK. Situated in the former home of House of Spells, it boosted the brand’s London presence with seven (make that six now, given the Soho announcement) standalone stores and nine London locations overall, including dedicated spaces within Harrods and Hamleys.
Ian Ashton, Head of UK Retail at Pop Mart, said: "The growth of our London community has been incredible, and this store is a reflection of that momentum. Charing Cross Road is more than a retail space - it’s where the Pop Mart universe comes to life, bringing together collectors, creativity and culture in one destination. This opening is about giving our community a home, while inviting new fans to discover what makes Pop Mart so unique."
Opening under the theme Step Into the Magic, the location introduces the Twinkle Twinkle Fairground, an immersive experience designed to spark curiosity and bring Pop Mart’s characters to life.

items.body:
Accenture veteran William McGrath takes on Head of Food WMS Food Transformation role at Sainsbury's
William McGrath is starting a new position as Head of Food WMS Transformation at Sainsbury's. He joins from Accenture where he spent 13 years, most recently serving as Senior Manager.
Facewatch
Sainsbury's plans to continue with its roll-out of Facewatch facial recognition technology to approximately 200 stores during 2026, despite a customer being wrongly challenged as a shoplifter and asked to leave a store earlier this month.
A Sainsbury's spokesperson said that this resulted from human error rather than a false match by the Facewatch system and that the retailer contacted the customer to apologise for his experience. "The incident was caused by human error, not the facial recognition technology. Customers can be reassured that the Facewatch system has a 99.98% accuracy rate, and every match is reviewed by a trained manager,” they added.
A Facewatch spokesperson commented: "We can confirm that our live facial recognition technology was not at fault in this incident. A correct alert was sent to the retailer, but was subsequently subject to human error in the way it was handled and communicated by the retailer."
Matt Arnold, 46, was buying items at a Sainsbury’s store in East Dulwich when he was stopped by management at a self-service checkout. He was waiting for a staff member to approve an alcohol purchase. Having scanned his items alongside his Nectar loyalty card, he waved an attendant over, but was instead approached by management.
"They came over and said I had to leave. The staff member said I'd been identified by the AI, and the cameras had flagged me," he told BBC London. "A shoplifter does not walk around with that much shopping, they don't scan it through, they don't put their Nectar card through. But what upset me was thinking this is what the future could be - people just listen to what the machine tells them to do without thinking about the consequences."
After being escorted off the premises, Arnold said he had looked back from the entrance and saw an overhead CCTV monitor alert with a red circle surrounding his face.

Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

items.body:
64 per cent of shoppers hate bad bots: how agentic voice is fixing retail’s AI trust crisis
Online shoppers everywhere know the frustrating feeling of hitting a digital dead end on an e-commerce site. You might be trying to track down an urgent package delivery or change a shipping address before an order leaves the warehouse, only to get trapped in an endless loop with an unhelpful automated chatbot.
You try rephrasing your question three different ways, but the screen just keeps spitting back the exact same useless menu choices over and over again.
Such continuing tension has resulted in a trust crisis between customers and e-commerce stores. Recent data regarding customer experiences reveals that 74% of shoppers feel annoyed with having to enter the same details again and again on different channels, while 64% will completely abandon a particular brand due to multiple negative automated experiences.
At the same time, behind the scenes, automated traffic is overwhelming e-commerce platforms, with 64% of bot attacks on retail specifically targeting API business logic. Between malicious scrapers holding inventory hostage and rigid legacy chatbots failing at basic communication, shoppers and retailers alike are paying the price for bad automation.
Retailers are caught in an awkward position. Contemporary consumers have become accustomed to receiving prompt and uninterrupted responses, whereas the current rule-based chatbots have created a lot of distrust on the part of the consumer. To address the trust deficit, progressive companies are gradually phasing out static decision trees in favour of more intelligent agentic voice technologies.
The Problem with Yesterday's Retail Bots
In the past, retail automation used simple decision trees. If the customer asked a question that fit within one of the predefined keywords, the bot would provide an automated response. However, if the customer asked a question that didn’t fall under one of the predefined rules, the entire system became perplexed.
This old design created three major headaches for retail brands:
- Zero Problem-Solving Ability: Traditional bots cannot talk directly to warehouse inventory databases or order management tools, meaning they cannot fix real problems on the fly.
- Constant Repetition: Shoppers are regularly forced to repeat their order details multiple times when an automated screen finally transfers them over to a live support team member.
- Cold and Robotic Tone: Flat, mechanical voices take all the warmth out of customer service, leaving buyers feeling like an annoying ticket number instead of a valued customer.
In situations where a customer faces issues like a delayed delivery of their parcel or an unexpected billing charge, a non-responsive response is viewed as an insult. Such negative customer experiences can drive customers away to the competition.
Enter Agentic Voice: Automation That Actually Listens
Voice technologies using the agentic voice concept adopt a whole new way of doing business. Unlike other technologies, where customers have to endure the frustration of pressing buttons through the telephone to get assistance or even wait for salespeople to help them out, agentic systems understand what humans are saying and execute actions accordingly.
Rather than giving static canned replies, an agentic voice system connects straight into a retailer's backend business tools. It can check a buyer's recent order history, look up live warehouse stock levels, and process product exchanges in just a few seconds.
For growing e-commerce teams handling high call volumes, using Murf 's AI voice agent enables online stores to offer clear, conversational phone support that handles complex customer questions without making callers wait on hold. The system speaks naturally, understands everyday human phrasing, and resolves routine customer requests right away.
If the process of automation is smooth, then customers will never complain. All queries of the shoppers are answered within seconds, while the support team is relieved of answering the same questions day by day.
How Intelligent Voice Agents Rebuild Brand Trust
Rebuilding consumer trust isn't about hiding technology from customers; it is about making sure the technology actually solves their problems quickly. Modern customer experience benchmarks highlight that over 80% of consumers now view intelligent AI as a standard expectation for fast service. Here is how modern retailers are using agentic voice to meet those expectations and build better customer relationships:
- Instant Resolution Without the Hold Music: In situations where there are holiday rushes or flash sales, the customer service line becomes congested in no time. Rather than letting buyers queue up for long periods, the voice agents answer their calls and solve their problems right away.
- Natural, Context Aware Conversations: Real human speech is full of pauses, quick corrections, and mid-sentence changes. Advanced voice agents follow complex phrasing effortlessly. If a customer says, "I want to swap the blue sweater in my cart for a green one, but only if it arrives by Friday," the system understands every part of that request and acts on it right away.
- Smooth Handoffs to Human Staff: When there is a need for human decision-making in a particular situation, say sorting out a complex case of return issues, the voice agent sends the entire conversation transcript to the live support agent. This way, the human agent joins in with all the background information in front of him.
Moving Beyond the Bad Bot Era
Retail technology has reached an important turning point. Online shoppers are no longer willing to tolerate rigid, unhelpful automated tools that waste their time and ruin their shopping experience. By replacing clunky decision-tree bots with responsive, action oriented voice intelligence, e-commerce brands can give buyers the immediate, human-sounding support they expect.

items.body:
Milestone for Ocado Retail as Profound bags $1.8bn valuation: last week's most read retail technology articles
Check out our most clicked retail technology articles from last week, including Tesco, Uber Eats, The Entertainer, THG Commerce, M&S, Azoma, Waitrose, Trust Retail, Complir, and RTIH's latest Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List.
Azoma lands investment from dunnhumby ventures to accelerate roadmap for agentic commerce platform
Azoma’s Agentic Commerce Optimisation platform, which measures and improves how AI shopping agents discover, interpret and recommend products for retailers and CPG brands, has announced an undisclosed investment from dunnhumby ventures.
As part of this, dunnhumby will be able to extend how it supports its retailer clients in optimising their customer facing chat agents while providing brands with ability to boost their discoverability and relevance in the new agentic commerce ecosystem The new funds will accelerate Azoma's product roadmap for customers including L'Oréal, Unilever and Mars, with a view to extending its ability to connect AI visibility to recommended actions and measuring incremental revenue.
Redefining the omnichannel landscape: RTIH's latest Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List goes live
The latest edition of the RTIH Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List is here! The list has seen a surge in popularity over the past few years, to the point that we’ve decided publishing it once a year is no longer enough. Here, then, is the second edition for 2026, with some names dropping out of the top 100 and some new names coming in (the latter are flagged as new entries for ease of reference).
Including the likes of retailers, brands, technologists, analysts, and consultants, the list celebrates individuals who are helping to redefine retail in a fast moving omnichannel age.
We use a variety of sources to select our top 100, including feedback from industry observers, research within our own networks, direct or third–party nominations via our website, and social media tools. In addition to social presence, we also take into account award winners and judges, event speakers, books published, media appearances, and people building innovative companies, solutions etc in the retail space.
We hope you enjoy reading through the top 100 and, as always, if you would like to give feedback or believe that there are some glaring omissions, please feel free to get in touch.
Many thanks to 3D Cloud, which provides 3D product visualisation software trusted by top furniture and DIY retailers, for sponsoring the list.
AI platform for marketing Profound follows The Estée Lauder Companies deal with $180 million Series D raise
Profound has raised a $180 million Series D at a $1.8 billion valuation, co-led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins, as it builds an AI platform for marketing.
“Two years ago we bet that people would stop clicking blue links and ask AI for the answer. It happened. The agent is now the customer. It scans hundreds of thousands of sources to form an opinion of your brand, and it wants all content current and specific,” says says James Cadwallader, CEO and Co-founder, Profound.
He adds: “Winning in AI search means being everywhere, all at once. It's an inhuman amount of work, and the only way to do it is with agents. That's why we built your AI Marketer, powered by Context Manager. Your AI Marketer is a marketing expert that proactively investigates your data, identifies opportunities, and then does the work while you stay in the loop. Context Manager is the system of record for your marketing context. It turns your meetings, threads, and brand data into one shared, permissioned understanding of your brand, plus a personal layer for how you work. This context is the antidote to slop, so as your brand evolves, so does your AI Marketer.”
“Today, more than 2,500 brands, including a third of the Fortune 100, do their marketing in Profound. Profound lives at the application layer, meaning your AI Marketer can harness the raw intelligence of Fable this week and Astra next week. And CMO's can audit, govern, and meter its work. I speak to CMOs every day and the expectation of what AI should do for marketing has changed completely. Yet frontier intelligence keeps going to code, finance and law. Engineers have Cognition. Lawyers have Harvey. Marketers… have been left in the lurch. Profound is expanding our applied AI research team to post-train models for marketing and build the first benchmark for real-world marketing tasks. More coming on that soon.”
The Entertainer partners with THG Commerce with focus on boosting its digital customer experience
UK toy retailer, The Entertainer, has appointed THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, as its new digital commerce partner. The multi-year tie up will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital experience, with the aim of creating a more intuitive, inspiring and personalised journey for families, gift buyers and adult toy and collectible enthusiasts.
THG Commerce will deploy AI enabled shopping assistance, conversational discovery and intent led search capabilities to help customers explore thousands of products and find the right choice more intuitively. These capabilities draw on the wider THG Ingenuity collaboration with Google Cloud, which harnesses Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini.
Alongside smarter search and discovery, the new experience will bring together richer content, curated product journeys and personalised recommendations to inspire customers throughout the purchasing journey. THG Commerce will deliver a new web and mobile experience, together with an enhanced Click & Collect journey designed to create a more seamless connection between digital discovery and The Entertainer’s nationwide store network.
The new platform is expected to launch in spring 2027 and has been designed to provide a foundation for future opportunities across loyalty, retail media and social commerce as The Entertainer continues to develop its omnichannel customer proposition.
Danish startup Complir lands $11 million in seed funding for AI tech being used by Flying Tiger Copenhagen
Copenhagen-based startup Complir, an AI infrastructure platform helping retailers and consumer brands manage product compliance across international markets, has announced a $11 million seed round.
The investment - led by General Catalyst alongside angel investors and specialist industry funds - will support its commercial expansion and go-to-market efforts, alongside investment in engineering and product development, and its teams. It follows the company’s $2 million pre-seed round in December 2025.
The platform is being used by the likes of Flying Tiger, Konges Sløjd, Matas Group and COOP Trading.
Mathilde Blander Bjerregaard at Flying Tiger, says: “There is a built in ‘need for speed’, especially in a seasonal business like ours. We can only deliver on time if we have 100% control over compliance for every single market.”
Thomas Ernfeldt, Chief Operating Officer at Konges Sløjd, says: “Complir has transformed the way we manage product compliance. It replaces a significant amount of manual work with a more streamlined and transparent process, freeing our teams to focus their time on quality assurance and product development while ensuring our products meet the necessary requirements.”
The clock is ticking: there are now just two weeks left to get your entries in for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
The eighth edition of the RTIH Innovation Awards is now up and running with the deadline for entries being Friday, 2nd October. That’s just two weeks away, so don’t delay, start working on your submissions today!
The awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027, celebrate global tech innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our latest winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Click here for FAQs, categories, and information on our judging panel.
Sign up for an account and submit your entry or entries here.
Ocado Retail reports online grocery delivery milestone as company hits 600,000 orders in one week
Ocado Retail, part of grocery technology and retail specialist Ocado Group and the operator of Ocado.com, a joint venture with Marks and Spencer, has racked up 600,000 orders in a single week.
In a LinkedIn post, the venture said: "What a week! Reaching a milestone of this scale takes incredible dedication, teamwork, and effort from every single person across our business. To mark the achievement, we brought the celebration into the office with plenty of team spirit, decorations, sweet treats, and a competition giving colleagues the chance to win even more Ocado goodies!"
Reaching over 80% of the UK population, Ocado lays claim to more than one million active customers and a range of around 50,000 products (including big name brands, over 7,000 items from the M&S food and drink range and Ocado’s Own-Range).
To put the 600,000 milestone in context, UK market leader Tesco currently handles over 1.2 million online grocery orders each week.
M&S opens doors to new Food store at Bell Green Retail Park in South East London
Marks and Spencer (M&S) has opened a new Food store at Bell Green Retail Park, near Lower Sydenham train station in South East London. This follows the launch of a new Food store in the same part of London, opposite Tooting Broadway station in May, and will be followed by another one at Elephant & Castle later this year.
The Bell Green location will open from 8am-9pm Monday to Saturday, and 10.30am-4.30pm on Sundays.
Alex Freudmann, Managing Director of M&S Food, says: “In this new phase of our transformation, we are reinvesting for growth and in London that means opening new Food stores with the right range for families, commuters and local residents. Whether that's our 140+ products in our Remarksable Value range, each benchmarked to market prices at M&S quality, or our innovations in Food on the Move, we are bringing the best of M&S to every London customer."
The Elephant & Castle location will be part of the Elephant Development, a £1.5 billion regeneration scheme. M&S says it expects these openings, alongside the move of its Tottenham Court Road store in Central London to a bigger location, to create 150 new jobs in the capital.
The retailer is opening four new Food stores across London and refurbishing six existing sites as part of its wider London expansion plans.
Tesco and Uber Eats launch Doorbell Drops delivery servcie with discounts on offer for Clubcard members
Running through to 20th September, Tesco and Uber Eats are launching Doorbell Drops, an exclusive selection of hosting essentials available at half-price to Clubcard members.
Customers can visit the Doorbell Drops hub page for Tesco on the Uber Eats app to shop the likes of Tesco Finest All Butter Sultana Scones, alongside strawberry jam and clotted cream, Mcvities Chocolate Digestives, Président French Brie with Jacobs crackers and Tesco Green Olives with Slow Roasted Tomatoes.
Merve Basci, Uber Eats UK General Manager, says: "Unannounced visits used to be a staple of British social and community life, but the fear of being unprepared and judged for stale biscuits is driving many to hide rather than host. Whether it’s dodging in-laws or frantically scouring the fridge for something edible to serve, our new partnership with Tesco can help people ditch the ‘doorbell dread’, so that young people especially can relax and enter their hosting era with more confidence."
Suzanne Quinn, Tesco Customer Director, says: “We’re always looking for little helps that make life easier for customers, and expanding our rapid delivery service through our Uber Eats partnership is another way we’re helping the nation get what they need, when they need it. The Doorbell Deals range has been created for those moments when plans change or guests arrive at short notice, giving customers quick access to fresh food, drink, and hosting essentials, so they can conveniently pull together a delicious spread in minutes.”
The launch follows Tesco’s recent partnership with Uber Eats, with the aim of extending rapid grocery delivery, Clubcard Prices and Clubcard points to more customers across the UK.
Waitrose keeps the faith with Trust Retail through to 2031 as inventory tech roll-out expands
Waitrose has extended its partnership with Trust Retail, a Trust Payments business, for a further five years, taking the relationship through to November 2031 as the supermarket prepares to accelerate the roll-out of Trust Retail’s inventory management technology across its store estate.
The technology was first trialled in a Waitrose store in March 2026 and is now live across eight stores. A wider roll-out is scheduled to begin at the end of September, with approximately 125 stores expected to be live before Christmas and the remaining Waitrose estate scheduled to follow by March 2027.
Trust Retail’s inventory management technology gives Waitrose partners a real-time view of stock, replacing processes that previously relied on batch updates. Transactions are reflected immediately across connected inventory and accounting systems, providing a more accurate and up-to-date view of stock throughout the trading day.
Using handheld devices, store partners can access current inventory information to support day-to-day activities including replenishment, stock management and markdown decisions.

items.body:
TALA has been on a rocket ship since its founding in 2019 by entrepreneur Grace Beverley. Built on largely organic social, TALA is entering its next stage of growth. It is set to open its third UK store and first outside London at Westfield St James Quarter, Edinburgh, in November 2026, following the success of its stores on Carnaby Street and at Westfield White City.
The move marks TALA’s first step into regional retail, following weeks of teasing on the brand’s social channels that had customers speculating on where the brand would land next.
The new Edinburgh store will showcase the brand’s full product range, offering customers an immersive brand experience with a personalised service, building on the learnings from both London locations.
Commenting on the expansion, TALA’s CEO, Sally Hughes-Daniels, said: “We’re proud to announce that TALA is opening its third store and first outside of London. The success of our Carnaby and Westfield White City stores has proven our retail model and it’s now time to build on this success. Expanding beyond London has long been in the works, but for our first step outside the capital it was so important that we found a location that felt a natural fit for TALA, and Edinburgh ticks every box.
We already know we have a great TALA community in Edinburgh, and the city’s strong outdoor and active culture makes it the perfect place for us to put down roots.
Bringing TALA to women all around the UK is one of our key goals, and we’re looking forward to Edinburgh marking the start of that IRL journey. We can’t wait to meet more of our community in person and become part of this historic city.”

items.body:
Gen Z gives High Street a boost by flocking to TikTok-famous stores
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Gen Z customers are giving the High Street a welcome lift by travelling up to an hour-and-a-half to visit independent shops made famous online.
The findings suggest stores suffering from the switch to e-commerce could gain a new lease of life through social media.
Research showed 80 per cent of Gen Z consumers, those born between 1997 and 2012, had visited an independent shop after finding it on sites such as Instagram and TikTok, credit card giant American Express revealed – even if it took 95 minutes to get there.
Businesses benefiting include Randalls sweet seller in Market Harborough, Leicestershire, and Humble Crumble, a pudding shop in London’s Borough Market.
Dan Edelman, at Amex, said: ‘Social media discovery is translating directly into visits and spending with small, independent firms.
With its growing influence and spending power, Gen Z is showcasing new opportunities for businesses to boost revenue, build loyalty and bring more people to Britain’s high streets.’
TikTok impact: Gen Z customers are giving the High Street a welcome lift
The findings on the ‘viral pilgrimage’ economy shed light on the behaviour of youngsters who can sometimes be seen congregating at certain shops, cafes or restaurants.
They showed 62 per cent of Gen Z consumers actively look up businesses on social media before visiting and 58 per cent say it led them to a firm they would not otherwise have found.
Most visit within a week of first seeing it online and one in five plan a day out around such a trip.
Consultancy Retail Economics found independent businesses captured half of ‘social-influenced High Street spending’ by Gen Z.

items.body:
Co-op has launched its newest store to serve and support the Norfolk market town of Attleborough, including a focus on incorporating and showcasing the latest sustainability features in its efforts to demonstrate and drive innovation as part of Co-op’s ongoing commitment to responsible retailing.
The store team were joined by the head teacher and pupils from the nearby Rosecroft Primary School, who helped to cut the ribbon and declare the new store open to serve the community. The pupils had also designed ‘sustainability themed’ bunting as part of the launch.
Located in London Road, Attleborough, the store opens between 7am-10pm daily offering Co-op’s extensive range and choice of fresh and chilled products; in-store bakery, hot food and, Costa Coffee Express. This sits alongside Co-op’s focus on meal deals and food to go; Fairtrade products; ready meals and meal ideas – including Co-op’s new Indian-inspired ‘Served’ range; pizzas; fresh meats and dairy; chilled beers and wines, fresh flowers and, everyday essentials.
Co-op’s latest ‘sustainability showcase store’ has been designed to communicate and share the sustainability initiatives that often go unnoticed behind the scenes, helping members and customers better understand the positive impact of everyday store operations. Measures range from motion activated fridge lights to water efficient fixtures, which are all built into the store design.
The new store – which has created 10 local jobs – will be utilised as a ‘test, learn and adopt’ environment allowing new sustainability technologies to be trialled, with the potential to roll-out and scale across Co-op’s wider estate. This includes coffee pod and soft plastic recycling services, making it easier for residents in the community to recycle, with soft plastic recycling allowing residents to return and recycle materials not widely accepted via household kerbside recycling.
EV charging points are also available, allowing vehicle charging whilst customer’s shop.
An InPost Locker is available for convenient parcel collection services, which can help to reduce mileage in last-mile logistics by consolidating multiple deliveries into a single stop and eliminate repeat door-to-door trips from missed deliveries.
The site also features nature-positive features such as wildflower meadow and bird-nesting bricks, helping to support local biodiversity and species such as sparrows and swifts.
Alex Ball, Co-op’s area manager, said: “We are delighted to invest in Attleborough, and proud to launch Co-op’s newest store and, latest sustainability showcase location – the store looks fantastic. We invest to create local stores which are more than just a shop, they are a hub contributing to local life and meeting the needs of communities. We have a focus on offering quality products, value and choice that can be enjoyed by everyone along with a range of added services. In addition, as a showcase store, we demonstrate our sustainability work in action – often going unnoticed behind the scenes, in-store communications inform our members and customers on the impactful changes we are making in our stores to help us on the important journey to net-zero”.
“We’re proud to serve Attleborough, and look forward to welcoming the community as they pop into their new Co-op. We’re here to contribute to local life and conveniently serve and support the community.”
There are offers, deals and promotions throughout the store for everyone. Member price savings create additional value for Co-op members who can save more with lower prices on the everyday essential products shoppers buy most.
Committed to backing British agriculture, all of Co-op’s own meat, poultry and dairy is 100% British – including in its pies, ready meals and sandwiches. Fairtrade products are available across the store supporting farmers, workers and their communities around the world who grow and produce products and ingredients for Co-op. Co-op’s own-brand water also supports clean water and sanitation projects in some of the world’s poorest communities through Co-op’s partnership with The One Foundation – Co-op donates 3p for every litre of own-brand water sold to the charity.
With its history dating back more than 180 years, Co-op is one of the world’s largest consumer-owned co-operatives. Co-op exists to create value for its membership and communities, its more than 7 million members own the business and play an intrinsic part in the governance of the organisation.
Co-op has reduced greenhouse gas emissions from its own operations by 65% since 2016, its longer-term target is to be a Net Zero business by 2035 across its own operations*, and by 2040 across its value chain**.
More information about the benefits of Co-op Membership is available by visiting coop.co.uk/membership

items.body:
Edinburgh shoppers are in for a treat as outdoor retailer Mountain Warehouse has officially opened the doors to its newest store at the Hermiston Gate Retail Park on Saturday, 12th September.
The store spans 8,705 square feet across one floor, featuring a wide range of affordable, quality outdoor clothing and equipment for all the family. Visitors can browse best-sellers, including walking boots, waterproof jackets, camping kit, and other essentials for all types of outdoor adventures.
Shoppers can also expect to find the active lifestyle brand Animal’s range of products within the store.
Mountain Warehouse founder, Mark Neale, said: “We’re excited to bring our passion for adventure to Edinburgh’s residents and visitors with the opening of our new store.”
The launch is part of Mountain Warehouse’s wider business expansion plans, following record sales in its latest annual results, driven by new stores and relocations. The retailer is also set to continue its growth with new openings and relocations across the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Poland, and Canada in the following year.

Grand Tour fans will be able to bid to own three of Jeremy Clarkson's personal cars from the hit TV show.
Nostalgic motorheads will be particularly keen to own the Lancia Montecarlo Spider driven by the TV star in the final ever episode of Amazon's motoring show.
His Alfa Romeo GTV6 and Lincoln Continental Mark V are also going under the hammer, making up the trio of wheels Clarkson is selling from his personal collection.
Eager viewers of Clarkson's Farm – the reality series that follows his attempts to run a farm in the Cotswolds – will find out the reason for the cars' sale in the forthcoming series.
The three vehicles will go on sale on Saturday, November 14 at the NEC Classic Motor Show and will be sold by Iconic Auctioneers.
Jeremy Clarkson said: 'I rarely get a chance these days to drive or enjoy these very special and quite famous cars so it’s probably for the best if they end up with someone who can.'

Within Clarkson's personal car collection, the 1982 Lancia Montecarlo Spider – an Italian mid-engined alternative to the Ferrari 308 – has a particularly significant place as it was the very last car he drove on The Grand Tour, marking a special moment of the TV presenter's career on screen.
Finished in Lotus Blue, it was his choice for The Grand Tour: One for the Road, the final episode featuring Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May together as lead presenters.
The famous trio drove across Zimbabwe and into Botswana, where Clarkson was unexpectedly reunited with the Lancia Beta Coupé he had driven in the 2007 Top Gear Botswana Special.
For One for the Road, the Montecarlo was modified with Ferrari 308 rear lights and quad tailpipes, Lancia Delta Integrale wheels, headlights and grille, cloth seats and a simple Alcantara-covered race-style steering wheel.
After filming, Clarkson bought the car himself and added it to his collection. It has since been tidied by Max500 Ltd and today starts, runs and drives well.

items.body:
Walker’s Shortbread, the trusted, family-run bakery that has been baking ‘Scotland’s finest’ for 128 years, has announced the launch of its new, limited-edition Queen’s Commemorative Tin in the global travel retail market. Exclusive to Avolta, the product is available now in its World Duty Free stores across UK airports.
The beautifully designed, golden tin features a classic black and white portrait of a young Queen Elizabeth II, adorned with her crown and jewellery, making it a unique collector’s item for travellers and admirers of the Royal Family. Inside, it holds Walker’s all butter assorted shaped shortbreads – including crown rounds, union jack shortbread and Walker’s famous shortbread fingers – still baked in the heart of the Highlands using only four quality ingredients: butter, flour, sugar and a pinch of salt.
The launch honours Walker’s ongoing connection with the Royal Family, with King Charles III (then Prince Charles, Duke of Rothesay) opening the Aberlour factory in 2001 and Walker’s head office, Aberlour House, in 2008. The company was also granted a Royal Warrant of Appointment from His Majesty King Charles III in 2024 for the supply of shortbread and oatcakes. This followed the granting of Royal Warrants from the late Queen Elizabeth II in 2017 and the Queen Mother in 2002, reflecting a history of royal recognition that underscores the brand’s unwavering commitment to the highest standards of quality.
Bryony Walker, commercial director at Walker’s Shortbread, said: “Our new commemorative tin reflects Walker’s long-standing association with the Royal Household and the craftsmanship behind our Scottish heritage. We are delighted to partner with Avolta to offer this exclusive collector’s item to passengers in travel retail. It represents a piece of Scottish heritage and a celebration of a remarkable legacy, allowing travellers to take home a gift that is both meaningful and delicious.”
Eve Fifer, commercial director in the UK at Avolta, said: “Products with a strong sense of place are an important part of the travel retail experience, particularly when they combine local heritage with a distinctive gifting opportunity. Walker’s is synonymous with Scottish provenance, and this limited-edition commemorative tin brings together the brand’s heritage, craftsmanship and iconic shortbread in a format created especially for travellers. We are pleased to offer it exclusively through our World Duty Free stores across UK airports.”
The launch arrives during a milestone year for the brand, coinciding with Walker’s recently being honoured with the prestigious King’s Award for Enterprise – a distinction that recognises its ongoing excellence in international trade.
The Queen’s Commemorative Tin (300g) is perfectly positioned as a premium keepsake. Inside, it contains Walker’s shortbread – an all-butter, indulgent treat, perfect for enjoying on the go, at home, or to share with family and friends. The limited-edition tin is available now at an RRP of £15.50.

items.body:
Deann Evans says farewell to e-commerce giant Shopify after five year Europe focused run with company
Deann Evans has announced her departure from Shopify where she served as Managing Director, EMEA. She joined the company five years ago, having previously worked at the likes of GoToDigital, Mettrr, and Sizmek.
In a LinkedIn post, in which she did not reveal her next career move, she said: “Over the past four weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to step back, spend valuable time with my family, and reflect on what comes next. After five incredible years at Shopify, I am leaving the company.”
She added: “I’m immensely proud of what this team has accomplished during that time. Together, we’ve strengthened Shopify’s presence across Europe, grown our partner ecosystem, and brought new products and opportunities to merchants across the region. When I joined, Shopify was best known in Europe as the platform for small businesses. Today, it supports everyone from first time founders to some of the world’s largest enterprises. But entrepreneurship will always be in the company’s DNA.”
The opportunity ahead is significant, Evans believes. “AI is changing how people discover and buy products, and Shopify merchants are ready for this new era of agentic commerce. With more than one billion products structured for discovery in the Shopify Catalogue and partnerships opening new ways to sell across major AI platforms Shopify is helping merchants of every size embrace the future of commerce.”
She concluded: “None of this happens without an exceptional team. Their talent, ambition, and deep commitment to merchants and partners will continue to drive Shopify’s success across Europe. I’m grateful to every merchant, partner, colleague, and leader who has been part of my journey. Thank you for the trust, collaboration, and many memorable moments along the way. I’m excited to discover what comes next for me, and I’ll be cheering on Shopify as it continues to play the long game.”
So hot right now
Shopify is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

Co-op Wholesale is setting its independent retail partners up for success by offering them more ways to win in the lucrative food-to-go category ahead of further anticipated market growth. ​ As part of its updated offering, Co-op Wholesale is working with partner Greencore to bring its direct-to-store (DTS) pricing and rebate in line with equivalent depot […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Co-op Wholesale is setting its independent retail partners up for success by offering them more ways to win in the lucrative food-to-go category ahead of further anticipated market growth. 
As part of its updated offering, Co-op Wholesale is working with partner Greencore to bring its direct-to-store (DTS) pricing and rebate in line with equivalent depot supply, making the service increasingly competitive to deliver greater value for retailers. 
Under the updated model, which takes effect from 5 October 2026, retailers will receive all the benefits of Greencore DTS at the same price as they would ordering from Co-op Wholesale’s depot, plus rebate will now apply (where applicable). The simplification and extension of this service will unlock multiple benefits around range, shelf life, waste, case size flexibility and cost for retailers, following feedback.
Forecast to be worth *£27bn by 2029 and currently valued at **£24.9bn, the category is key for convenience retailers and one that Co-op Wholesale has long maintained a sharp focus on. 
The Greencore DTS model creates opportunities for increased profit and reduces waste, through an additional day’s shelf life and the benefit of ordering in single pick via Greencore DTS.
Co-op Wholesale, which supplies its partners with the Co-op Brand product portfolio, is pleased to offer almost double the number of SKUs (85) via Greencore DTS. As well as Co-op Brand sandwiches, wraps, salads, pasta pots and sushi, additional brands including leading Japanese kitchen Yo Sushi lines are available to give both retailers and shoppers additional choice and access to a full variety of delicious food to go options. 
The award-winning Co-op Brand food to go offering, which exclusively consists of 100 per cent British meat and ethically sourced quality ingredients, is reflective of the latest trends, such as the Irresistible Parmesan Chicken Caesar Wrap, developed to drive sales and meet shoppers’ high expectations. 
Co-op Wholesale’s updated proposition has been strategically designed to meet this demand via the convenience channel, with ***71 per cent of consumers confirming they prefer quality over simply locating the cheapest option. 
Robbie Moore, Co-op Wholesale Trading Director, said: “We truly listen to what our partners tell us they want and this evolution of our food-to-go proposition is testament to that. They told us their businesses would benefit from larger ranges, longer shelf life and most of all, a streamlined rebate structure, so we’ve developed a solution and invested to support them. We’re looking forward to it going live in October.” 
*Source: Lumina Intelligence Food-To-Go Market Report 2026
