items.title: Chancellor must act to stem rising inflation, says BRC
items.summary: The latest CPI inflation figures show headline inflation rose to 2.9%, up by 31% in the 12 months to August, and food inflation remained unchanged at 1.3%. On a monthly basis, food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose by 0.4% in August 2026, the same rise… This story continues at Chancellor must act to stem rising inflation, says BRC Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
On a monthly basis, food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose by 0.4% in August 2026, the same rise as in August 2025.
In response, Harvir Dhillon, lead economist at the British Retail Consortium (BRC), said: “Today’s figures highlight the challenging environment retailers face. Headline inflation has increased, with goods such as clothing and accessories seeing marked increases on the month.
“One bright spot for households was that food inflation remained unchanged, with deals to be had on staple items like olive oil and coffee.
“By working to offer the most competitive prices, supermarkets have managed to shield their customers from the worst of the cost pressures feeding through the supply chain.
“Tackling the cost of living is a top priority and retailers continue to do all they can to hold prices down. But until fiscal conditions improve, they will be fighting with one hand tied behind their back.
“The Autumn Budget is a chance to reset and reduce the cost pressures building up across the industry. Business Rates are perhaps the most significant of these, with retailers paying a disproportionate share of the total rates bill.
“Rising inflation means that businesses will expect their rates bill to rise even faster in April, adding to the cost pressures already being felt from high energy bills, employment costs, and packaging fees.
“The chancellor can take meaningful action to mitigate these costs, using the Budget to announce a freeze to business rates. Halting the rise in these costs is the best way to support retailers, and by extension, the households who depend on them.”
Bogdan Toma, partner, McKinsey & Company, commented: “Petrol prices at their highest level in nearly four years could signal an uncertain ‘golden quarter’ for consumers and retailers. With households absorbing back-to-school costs and facing the possibility of higher interest rates, demand heading into the fourth quarter may remain subdued.
“The ‘golden quarter’ is critical to annual profitability for many non-food, and some grocery retailers.
“This year, competition for fewer and smaller baskets could be particularly intense, pressuring retailer margins from an already challenged starting point.”

items.body:
The Entertainer Partners with THG Commerce with focus on boosting its digital customer experience
UK toy retailer, The Entertainer, has appointed THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, as its new digital commerce partner. The multi-year tie up will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital experience, with the aim of creating a more intuitive, inspiring and personalised journey for families, gift buyers and adult toy and collectible enthusiasts.
THG Commerce will deploy AI enabled shopping assistance, conversational discovery and intent led search capabilities to help customers explore thousands of products and find the right choice more intuitively. These capabilities draw on the wider THG Ingenuity collaboration with Google Cloud, which harnesses Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini.
Alongside smarter search and discovery, the new experience will bring together richer content, curated product journeys and personalised recommendations to inspire customers throughout the purchasing journey. THG Commerce will deliver a new web and mobile experience, together with an enhanced Click & Collect journey designed to create a more seamless connection between digital discovery and The Entertainer’s nationwide store network.
The new platform is expected to launch in spring 2027 and has been designed to provide a foundation for future opportunities across loyalty, retail media and social commerce as The Entertainer continues to develop its omnichannel customer proposition.
Malcolm Carter, Digital & Marketing Director, The Entertainer, says: “Our ambition is to redefine the experience for anyone looking to discover and buy toys, whether they are shopping for their children, choosing a gift for someone else or buying for themselves. Toy shopping should be joyful and inspiring, but the sheet breadth of choice means customers increasingly need help navigating it.”
“We have a real opportunity to combine the expertise, trusted brands and passion for play people associate with The Entertainer with intelligent technology that helps customers find something they’ll love. Partnering with THG Commerce gives us the technology, capability and ambition to reimagine that experience across digital, stores and wherever our customers choose to shop in an increasing AI centric landscape. This is an important investment in the next generation of The Entertainer and in how we serve our customers.”
Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity, says: “The Entertainer is one of the most recognisable names in UK toy retail. Toy retail is a particularly rich discovery environment. Customers arrive with very different missions, from gifting and family purchases to collecting, and technology can play a powerful role in helping them navigate choice and discover the right products.”
“The Entertainer get AI enabled shopping assistance and CRM integrated enhanced personalisation at launch, then a roadmap into loyalty, retail media and social commerce, backed by our wider THG Studios capabilities which can bring a new range to life on site quickly. We have built our AI capabilities to work anywhere, as standalone services that integrate with any commerce platform, so brands can benefit from them whether or not they replatform with us. We look forward to working closely with The Entertainer team to support their long-term growth ambitions”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Digital experiences will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

items.summary: WH Smith has cut its profit target again after warning that intense discounting and “inflation headwinds” are hitting its bottom line. The convenience retailer had initially told investors it could make as much as £105m in pre-tax profit this year, before slashing the target to between £75m and £90m. On Wednesday, the group reduced its [...]
items.body:
WH Smith warns on profit again as discounting hits margins
WH Smith has cut its profit target again after warning that intense discounting and “inflation headwinds” are hitting its bottom line.
The convenience retailer had initially told investors it could make as much as £105m in pre-tax profit this year, before slashing the target to between £75m and £90m. On Wednesday, the group reduced its expectations to no higher than £75m.
“This reflects lower trading profit margins driven by increased promotional activity, a reduction in brand marketing and inflation headwinds, offset by central cost reductions and lower interest costs,” the firm said.
WH Smith has struggled to gain momentum following the sale of its 480 high street stores to private equity firm Modella Capital.
The group has been forced to rely on sales at its train station and airport stores, which it has said are vulnerable to the slowdown in tourism caused by the Iran war.
The retailer’s £75m expected profit would mark a sharp fall from last year’s £108m. Only a few months ago, the group took £103m in an equity raise designed to bolster its balance sheet and drive its investment plans.
WH Smith saw sales inch up during its fourth quarter, as summer trading pushed revenue growth up from one to two per cent across the group.
In the UK, like-for-like revenue growth jumped from two to four per cent in the fourth quarter. The group’s hospital stores drove this uplift, as like-for-like revenue jumped by eight per cent.
WH Smith ‘needs to rebuild credibility’
WH Smith said it refurbished its shops in Heathrow, Liverpool, Belfast International and East Midlands airports in a bid to drive up the size of shoppers’ baskets in these high-footfall sites.
The group’s performance in North America has dragged on its overall growth in recent years. Like-for-like revenue in the region dipped by three per cent in the fourth quarter.
The retailer’s like-for-like revenue at its North American airport stores dipped by two per cent, dragged down by lower passenger volumes and “softer consumer demand”.
In June, WH Smith’s share price shed 16 per cent in one day after it warned that the slump in consumer confidence and airport traffic caused by the Iran war is hitting its sales.
The firm said on Wednesday that it is making “good progress” towards its turnaround plan. The group told investors it is working to cut costs, improve its cash management and boost sales in its more profitable “travel essentials” range.
Analysts at RBC Capital Markets said WH Smith has posted better-than-expected UK results, but is performing worse than hoped in the North American market.
“We think WH Smith needs to rebuild credibility with the market, with scope for the rating to recover over time if WH Smith can reassure the market that its recent missteps won’t be repeated,” they said.
Shares in WH Smith opened broadly flat in early trading, at 359p.

items.title: Shoplifters carrying shopping lists, says M&S manager
items.summary: The Marks and Spencer area manager for Shropshire says shoplifting is a "really large issue".
items.body:
Shoplifters carrying shopping lists, says M&S manager
- Published
Shoplifters walk into branches of Marks & Spencer with a list in an attempt to get away with hauls worth thousands of pounds, a regional manager says.
Elisa Lewis, who is responsible for M&S shops in Shropshire, said shoplifting was a "really large issue" and could be "a daily, possibly even hourly, occurrence".
"In my experience it can be anybody," she said. "It can be a bored housewife who's just nicking a jacket for a bit of fun, and the people who we do catch are sometimes those we least expect."
Some shoplifters were people experiencing alcohol or drug dependence who said they were "just doing it to survive".
As a physically smaller woman, she said she found tackling some of them "intimidating", but had become more hardened to it through experience.
Figures collected by the BBC show a slight fall in the number of shoplifting offences across England and Wales in the past financial year and that was mirrored in the West Mercia police force area.
Marks and Spencer has a policy of issuing lifetime bans to shoplifters, which Lewis said could be a big deterrent and a big shock, especially to younger offenders.
But she said sometimes it turned out to be a genuine accident and they took people to their in-house detention room to try to understand their motivations before acting.
In some cases it is no accident though, and she said: "They've come in with a special order, and they go around stealing to order, and that can go into thousands of pounds depending on what people are asking for."
She said the run up to Christmas was always a peak time for shoplifting, with people wanting presents and money.
She also said the quieter times of the day tended to be the peak hours.
"Usually you find in your first hour of trade is where you get people who are reliant on money, drugs, etc," she said.
"They will head for your meat, your alcohol, your suits, because that's what they'll get the most money for."
Lewis said she had seen the level of shoplifting increase and decrease in line with the cost of living, but added: "When there is a presence in the town, they are deterred."
Insp Ingrid Tozer, the West Mercia Police officer responsible for Shrewsbury town centre, said an increased police presence there was making a difference.
Since October there have been six police officers and a sergeant based in the town, and she said incidents of shoplifting had fallen.
"The feedback has been fantastic," she said, and the force believed it had issued criminal behaviour orders to the most prolific offenders.
But engaging traders has been a challenge.
PC Joseph Bradley, one of the police officers based in Shrewsbury, said: "We spent quite a bit of time trying to encourage the shops to report thefts into us.
"We went through a period when we weren't necessarily getting a lot of reports in."
He has worked in the town for 16 years and said he had spent a lot of time building up relationships with traders to make that happen.
That was backed up by Cath Harmer from Shrewsbury BID - a group that represents businesses in the town.
She is the Safer Shrewsbury coordinator, responsible for the Shrewsbury Rangers, external - a security team which patrols the streets, assisting shopkeepers and the police.
Harmer said: "There is a tendency for retailers to absorb that theft rather than reporting it," and added she wanted to make sure they continued reporting crime.

GXO and Exotec announce automation partnership to boost fashion fulfilment for Guess in the Netherlands
GXO Logistics and Exotec have deployed Exotec’s Skypod system at GXO's Venlo, Netherlands, facility, home to fashion brand Guess. The installation includes 127 Skypod robots, 60,000 rack locations, eight goods-to-person picking stations and 200 metres of conveyor network. The system is also capable of processing up to 70,000 pieces per day, achieving throughput of up to 2,200 order lines per hour during peak periods.
With the deployment of the automated solution, GXO says it is enhancing fulfilment operations for Guess across EMEA and Asia by increasing throughput, improving productivity and supporting future growth.
Mark Donné, Operations Manager, GXO Venlo, says: "The impact has been evident from day one. Our automated solution with Exotec, tailored specifically for Guess, has helped take our operation to the next level, enabling faster processing, greater predictability and a smoother workflow across the site. As our business with Guess continues to grow, we have the scalability and flexibility needed to support future demand."
Wim Vermeir, Senior Sales Executive Benelux, Exotec, comments: "Fashion logistics doesn't tolerate approximation - high SKU counts, seasonal spikes, and EMEA wide distribution require precision engineering, not off-the-shelf automation. With GXO, we designed a system built specifically for those demands, and the throughput numbers speak for themselves. The result is a highly efficient operation that supports both current performance and future growth."

items.body:
Danish startup Complir lands $11 million in seed funding for AI tech being used by Flying Tiger Copenhagen
Copenhagen-based startup Complir, an AI infrastructure platform helping retailers and consumer brands manage product compliance across international markets, has announced a $11 million seed round.
The investment - led by General Catalyst alongside angel investors and specialist industry funds - will support its commercial expansion and go-to-market efforts, alongside investment in engineering and product development, and its teams. It follows the company’s $2 million pre-seed round in December 2025.
The platform is being used by the likes of Flying Tiger, Konges Sløjd, Matas Group and COOP Trading.
Mathilde Blander Bjerregaard at Flying Tiger, says: “There is a built in ‘need for speed’, especially in a seasonal business like ours. We can only deliver on time if we have 100% control over compliance for every single market.”
Thomas Ernfeldt, Chief Operating Officer at Konges Sløjd, says: “Complir has transformed the way we manage product compliance. It replaces a significant amount of manual work with a more streamlined and transparent process, freeing our teams to focus their time on quality assurance and product development while ensuring our products meet the necessary requirements.”
"Product compliance has become one of the biggest operational bottlenecks for global retailers," says Gustav Bang, Co-founder and CEO at Complir. “Companies are managing increasingly complex regulations across hundreds of thousands of products, yet much of the work is still performed manually. We're building the AI infrastructure that allows compliance, quality and regulatory teams to move faster, reduce risk, and bring products to market with confidence, and ultimately limit people’s exposure to dangerous products."
Samuel Beyer, Partner at General Catalyst, comments: "Product compliance is the gateway to global trade and the cornerstone of consumer trust, yet it remains one of the last areas of commerce stuck in the past still running on email threads and spreadsheets. Complir turns that scattered work into a single system of record, so compliance moves at the speed of the product roadmap instead of gating it. That's what lets companies compete globally while consumers can still trust the safety claim on the box."

Waitrose keeps the faith with Trust Retail through to 2031 as inventory technology roll-out expands
Waitrose has extended its partnership with Trust Retail, a Trust Payments business, for a further five years, taking the relationship through to November 2031 as the supermarket prepares to accelerate the roll-out of Trust Retail’s inventory management technology across its store estate.
The technology was first trialled in a Waitrose store in March 2026 and is now live across eight stores. A wider roll-out is scheduled to begin at the end of September, with approximately 125 stores expected to be live before Christmas and the remaining Waitrose estate scheduled to follow by March 2027.
Trust Retail’s inventory management technology gives Waitrose partners a real-time view of stock, replacing processes that previously relied on batch updates. Transactions are reflected immediately across connected inventory and accounting systems, providing a more accurate and up-to-date view of stock throughout the trading day. Using handheld devices, store partners can access current inventory information to support day-to-day activities including replenishment, stock management and markdown decisions.
Mike Dotson, Managing Director at Trust Retail, says: “Implementing inventory management technology across a retail environment of this scale is a complex undertaking, but our teams have worked closely together to understand Waitrose’s operational requirements, integrate the technology across its existing systems and create a solution that gives colleagues a more accurate, real-time view of stock. With the initial stores now live and the wider roll-out beginning, we’re excited to take the next step in the partnership and support Waitrose as it brings these capabilities to colleagues across its store estate. The lessons learned from this partnership will help us to deploy inventory management in any grocery and convenience retail premises moving forwards.”
Laurence Booth, Group CEO at Trust Payments, says: “Extending our partnership with Waitrose for a further five years is a substantial milestone and reflects the close collaboration that has underpinned this project from the outset.”
Stuart Gibbon, Product Lead, Stock & End-to-end End Programme at Waitrose & Partners, comments: “Having accurate and timely stock information is important to how our partners manage products across our stores and ultimately to the service we provide our customers.”
“As the technology rolls out more widely, it will give our teams greater visibility of stock and support faster, more informed decisions throughout the trading day. Trust Retail has worked closely with our teams to understand our requirements and how we operate. Extending the partnership gives us the continuity to build on the work already completed and support the next stage of the roll-out across our store estate.”

items.body:
NRF Europe 2026 star Hanshow: the Store Digital Twin will become the operating system for future retail
Introduction: the next frontier of retail AI
As the retail industry heads to NRF 2026: Retail’s Big Show Europe in September, much of the conversation continues to centre on artificial intelligence. From generative AI to emerging agentic commerce, retailers are exploring how AI can improve decision-making, streamline operations and create more responsive shopping experiences.
Yet a fundamental challenge remains. While AI has become increasingly capable of analysing information and generating recommendations, physical retail environments remain highly dynamic and complex. Products move, shelves change, store conditions evolve, and customer behaviour shifts continuously throughout the day. Understanding what is actually happening inside the store, and acting upon it in real time, remains one of the industry's greatest operational challenges.
As AI moves closer to the heart of store operations, the question is no longer simply how to deploy AI, but how to provide the operational foundation that enables AI to understand, interpret and act within physical retail environments. This is where Store Digital Twin is becoming increasingly important. More than a technology initiative, Store Digital Twin is emerging as the foundational operational platform that enables AI powered retail operations.
From visibility to autonomy: the evolution of retail operations
Store Digital Twin is becoming increasingly important as retailers seek to move beyond traditional approaches to store management. While early digital initiatives focused primarily on visibility, the next stage of retail transformation is about creating the conditions for smarter and more responsive operations.
The journey often begins with understanding what is happening across products, shelves, shoppers and store assets in real time. Once these signals are connected, retailers can begin identifying patterns, uncovering root causes and understanding why issues occur. This deeper level of insight creates the foundation for AI powered decision-making, enabling organisations to prioritise issues, evaluate business impact and determine the most appropriate actions.
The greatest value emerges when intelligence is connected directly to execution. Insights become operational outcomes through store teams, automated workflows and increasingly intelligent systems capable of coordinating actions across the retail environment. Over time, this creates a path towards greater operational autonomy, where sensing, analysis, decision-making and execution function as a continuous cycle of optimisation.
Viewed through this lens, the significance of Store Digital Twin lies not only in improving visibility, but in providing the platform that connects awareness, intelligence and execution. As AI becomes more deeply embedded within retail operations, the transition from visibility to autonomy is likely to become one of the defining themes of the industry's next phase of transformation.
For technology providers, this also requires a shift in focus. Rather than addressing individual operational challenges in isolation, the goal is increasingly to create an operational foundation where data, intelligence and execution work together within a unified framework. This thinking underpins Hanshow's approach to Store Digital Twin.
Building an AI powered Store Digital Twin ecosystem
At Hanshow, the Store Digital Twin is built through a connected ecosystem that links products, people, assets and operational processes across the store. At its core, a Store Digital Twin provides a real-time digital representation of store operations. More importantly, it creates the foundation that enables information, intelligence and execution to work together within a single operational environment.
At the frontline, Hanshow’s solutions such as NexShelf, NexConnect Smart Cart and NexMate robotics help create real-time awareness across the retail environment. Together, they provide visibility into product availability, shelf execution, shopper interactions and operational conditions within the store. By connecting information from multiple touchpoints, retailers gain a more complete understanding of how their stores are performing in real time.
Building upon this operational awareness, AI powered solutions such as xPilot help transform information into actionable intelligence. By analysing operational conditions, identifying issues and recommending next steps, AI can help store teams focus resources where they create the greatest impact, improving consistency and responsiveness across the store network.
At the same time, Store Digital Twin continues to expand beyond the sales floor itself. Store operations are increasingly influenced by critical infrastructure and energy systems, making operational visibility across these assets equally important. NexGrid and NexOptim solutions bring energy management, in-store systems and other critical store assets into a unified operational environment, helping retailers improve efficiency, resilience and sustainability.
Together, these capabilities contribute to a connected Store Digital Twin ecosystem where people, products, assets and operational processes are linked through a shared operational foundation. This foundation enables AI not only to observe the store, but also to support decision-making, coordinate execution and lay the groundwork for increasingly autonomous operations.
Case study: how Rainbow & Lingzhi built an AI ready operational model
Rainbow's collaboration with Hanshow provides a practical example of how Store Digital Twin can support AI enabled retail operations.
As one of China's leading digital retailers, Rainbow operates in one of the world's most competitive retail markets, where e-commerce, instant delivery and omnichannel competition continue to raise expectations for operational speed, efficiency and execution.
Rainbow has been exploring how to connect real-time operational awareness, intelligent decision-making and execution across its store network. Through the deployment of a Store Digital Twin ecosystem incorporating solutions such as NexShelf, NexConnect and xPilot, Rainbow has established a more connected operational environment capable of supporting data driven store management.
In an award winning joint initiative in merchandise precision management, Rainbow brings Store Digital Twin and AI powered intelligence into operations. One key application focuses on out-of-shelf (OOS) management. Hanshow provides the store-wide sensing hardware that captures real-time shelf images and inventory data, while Lingzhi contributes its self-developed AI analytics engine to interpret that data.
Together, the two capabilities enable continuous, around-the-clock monitoring of shelf availability - automatically identifying out-of-stock SKUs and pinpointing their exact locations. Lingzhi's demand forecasting algorithms then automatically issue replenishment tasks, helping store teams respond faster and more consistently. By connecting detection, analysis and task creation within a single workflow, the project helps reduce response times while improving product availability and operational efficiency.
Rainbow is also among the first retailers to deploy xPilot in live store environments. By introducing intelligence driven, automated workflows into daily operations, xPilot helps store teams respond more quickly to merchandising, pricing and inventory issues, reducing reliance on manual inspections and improving execution consistency across the store network.
More importantly, this co-developed operational model pioneered by Rainbow highlights a broader industry direction: the shift from deploying individual technologies to building a unified operational foundation capable of supporting AI powered retail execution.
Conclusion: the operating system for future retail
As retailers explore the next generation of AI powered operations, the conversation around Store Digital Twin is only just beginning. The next chapter of retail transformation will not be defined by visibility alone, but by how effectively retailers connect awareness, intelligence and execution across the physical store. As these capabilities become increasingly integrated, the path towards more autonomous operations becomes clearer.
At NRF 2026: Retail's Big Show Europe, Hanshow will showcase how its AI powered Store Digital Twin ecosystem is helping retailers establish a unified operational foundation for the future, creating the conditions for more intelligent, adaptive and increasingly autonomous store operations.
Visit Hanshow at Hall 6, Booth E-020, and follow Hanshow on LinkedIn for the latest insights on retail innovation.

Westfield Rise unveils new AI technology powered drive to store measurement capabilities for advertisers
Westfield Rise, Westfield's in-house retail media agency, has launched new audience measurement capabilities across Westfield London and Westfield Stratford City, with the aim of giving advertisers deeper insight into how campaigns influence attention, engagement and store visitation.
The launch is backed by data which found that shoppers exposed to advertising were 27% more likely to visit a brand's store than those who weren't exposed to a campaign. Additional findings include: experiential activations delivered an average dwell time of 1 minute and 28 seconds; nearly one in four visitors engaged with an activation for more than 60 seconds.
Developed in partnership with Digeiz, the measurement solution uses AI powered technology to analyse visitor journeys across shopping centres. The UK launch forms part of a wider roll-out of Westfield Rise’s audience measurement platform across 23 Westfield destinations in Europe.
Mel Lalou, Director of Westfield Rise, Northern Europe, says: “Brands are increasingly looking for greater accountability from every marketing investment, particularly as retail media becomes a more important part of the media mix. These enhanced measurement capabilities give advertisers a clearer understanding of how campaigns perform in physical retail environments, connecting audience exposure and attention with real-world behavioural outcomes, including store visitation and drive to store impact.”
Lalou adds: “Historically, measuring the impact of advertising in physical environments has been challenging. Consumers decide in real-time whether an experience is worth their attention, making experiential marketing one of the most authentic tests of brand relevance. Westfield Rise gives brands both the stage and the measurement to create experiences that genuinely resonate and drive action. Brands can now see not only who they reached, but also what shoppers did next. This provides a clearer link between media investment and real-world retail outcomes within our centres.”

items.body:
Returned and overstocked inventory specialist Buywander raises $21 million in Series A funding
Buywander, an auction-based marketplace for returned and overstocked retail inventory, has announced a $21 million Series A funding round, bringing the company's total funding to date to $28 million. The round was led by Madrona Venture Group and Inspired Capital. Previous backers include Triple Impact Capital, Silence Ventures, Data Tech Fund and Animal Capital, along with a group of angel investors.
"Retailers are sitting on billions of dollars in returned and overstocked inventory every year, and buyers are hungry for a better way to access it," says Jordan Allen, Co-Founder and CEO of Buywander. "We've seen that appetite play out in every market we've entered. This funding lets us bring that experience to more cities, faster, and introduce Buywander to more people who are excited to discover great products, compete for a win, and give returned goods a second life."
Buywander will use the cash to accelerate expansion across the US, invest in technology, and grow its leadership team, building on its eight locations including recent market launches in Denver, Chicago, and an upcoming opening in Minneapolis.
"Scaling this model market by market takes real infrastructure from warehouse operations to reverse logistics and retailer relationships," says Brock Kowalchuk, Co-Founder at Buywander. "This round lets us build that foundation ahead of demand, so every new market opens with the same reliability customers already expect from us in our existing markets."
Buywander also recently expanded its leadership team. This includes: Laura Sasser, Chief Operating Officer; Mani Sundaram, Chief Product Officer; Daniel Kiepfer, VP of Data and AI; Abu Marcose, Senior Director of Warehouse Technology; and Roger Ling, Director of Marketing. They join Srinivas Paluri, Chief Technology Officer; Brent Hendricks, VP of Strategic Operations; Rett Clevenger, VP of Merchandising; and Ark Rozycki, Chief Architect. As part of the round, Scott Jacobson, Alexa von Tobel, and Greg Greeley have joined Buywander's board of directors, while Charlotte Ross has joined as a board observer.
"Buywander is solving a problem that's only getting bigger. Retailers are drowning in returned and overstocked inventory, and there's never been a good local solution for moving it," says Alexa von Tobel, Founder and Managing Partner at Inspired Capital. "What stood out to us is how much traction the model has already found in every market it's entered. Jordan and Brock have built something that works for buyers, works for retailers, and scales city by city without losing the local warehouse experience that makes the model work."
"We've watched affordability go from a discount seeker habit to just how most people shop, and this shift isn't reversing anytime soon,” says Scott Jacobson, Managing Director at Madrona. “Jordan and Brock have built the first model that actually turns the trillion-dollar problem of retail returns into a scalable opportunity for value oriented shoppers. Almost every major retailer is sitting on this same supply problem, and there are just as many shoppers on the other side hunting for exactly this kind of deal, which is what Buywander serves so effectively."

items.body:
David’s Bridal taps AI technology to turn first-party wedding data into a new B2B growth platform
David’s Bridal, a North American bridal and occasion retailer and Pearl, its AI powered platform, have announced the launch of Pearl Connect, pitched as the first AI vendor platform native to a couple’s wedding planning journey, putting everything a professional in this space needs to market, communicate and book into one touchpoint.
“Wedding professionals shouldn’t have to spend their days chasing emails, piecing together details and wondering which leads are actually worth their time,” says Kelly Cook, CEO at David’s Bridal. “We know what couples are planning, what they’re looking for, and where they are in their journey.”
“Pearl Connect puts that context to work for the businesses on the other side of the aisle. We’re simplifying all those disjointed ways of connecting into one place with the goal of removing any friction so wedding professionals can have a more meaningful, real connection with potential couples. It’s a very different way to think about a wedding vendor marketplace - it’s about vendor listings, it’s about creating real connections that can lead to revenue and growth for wedding pros.”
“Pearl Connect is designed around a simple idea: a vendor should know more than a name and an email when a potential client reaches out,” adds Elina Vilk, President and Chief Business Officer at David’s Bridal. “When a couple comes through Pearl, we can connect that inquiry to the context they’ve already shared - their date, venue, style, budget, and what they’re actually looking for. That gives both sides a better starting point.”
“The couple doesn’t have to start over, and the vendor doesn’t have to spend the first several exchanges figuring out whether the opportunity is a fit. Together, Pearl Planner and Pearl Connect create a wedding planning flywheel: couples plan and share intent, vendors gain context around that intent, and both sides get a simpler path to a real connection and tangible business growth.”

Quadient expands UK parcel locker network through partnership with SPAR UK retailer James Hall Co.
Quadient has announced a partnership with James Hall & Co., SPAR UK’s primary retailer, wholesaler, and distributor for the North of England.
Parcel Pending by Quadient lockers are being rolled out across James Hall & Co.’s G&E Murgatroyd company owned retail estate, with 37 locations already live and further deployments planned across its network of stores. These offer 24/7 access for deliveries, returns, exchanges, and item storage. They support a range of services, including prescription collection, Click and Collect, key exchange, and spare parts retrieval.
“Through the company’s SPAR stores, partnering with James Hall & Co. Ltd allows us to further embed our open locker network into the fabric of local communities across the North of England,” says Katia Bourgeais-Crémel, EVP Parcel Locker Solutions Europe at Quadient. “Convenience retail plays a critical role in everyday life, and by introducing smart, secure lockers into these locations, we are removing friction from parcel collection and returns. This partnership reflects our focus on delivering predictable, scalable last-mile solutions that benefit the entire ecosystem from carriers and retailers to consumers and store staff.”
Fiona Drummond, Company Stores Director at James Hall & Co., says: “We are committed to enhancing the role our SPAR stores play within local communities, offering services that go beyond traditional retail. Partnering with Quadient enables us to introduce a secure and convenient parcel solution that meets the evolving needs of our customers, while driving additional footfall and value for our stores. We look forward to continuing the roll-out across our estate.”
Quadient’s locker network now spans the US, Japan, and Europe, with over 28,200 units installed globally and plans to reach 40,000 by 2030.

items.title: Boohoo owner Debenhams sells fashion label Nasty Gal to WSG Brands in £12m deal
items.summary: Debenhams boss Dan Finley described the business as 'non-core' and said the sale would help bolster its balance sheet amid a turnaround effort.
items.body:
Boohoo owner Debenhams sells fashion label Nasty Gal to WSG Brands in £12m deal
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Boohoo owner Debenhams has sold its Nasty Gal brand for just under £12million.
The online retailer, which changed its name from Boohoo last year, said it has sold the women’s fashion label to US firm WSG Brands.
Debenhams boss Dan Finley described the business as ‘non-core’ and said the sale would help bolster its balance sheet amid its turnaround effort.
The group had paid just under £15million to buy Nasty Gal out of bankruptcy in February 2017. It was founded by Sophia Amoruso as an Ebay shop that sold vintage items of clothes online when she was a student in California in the early 2000s.
Amoruso was named as one of the richest self-made women in the world in 2016 by Forbes but Nasty Gal’s fortunes soured after declining sales and costly lawsuits. Her early days founding the business were depicted in the Netflix series ‘Girl Boss’, based on her autobiography.
Celebrities including Emily Ratajkowski and Cara Delevingne launched fashion collaborations with the business.
Emily Ratajkowski launched a fashion range with Nasty Gal in 2019
But in recent years, Debenham’s youth brands – which also include Boohoo and PrettyLittleThing – have lost shoppers to ultra-cheap Chinese retailer, Shein, as well as resale platform Vinted.
Debenhams said Nasty Gal made £12million in sales and profits of £400,000 in its most recent financial year.
Finley said: ‘Our turnaround continues at pace. The disposal of this non-core asset aligns with our strategy and further strengthens the balance sheet following the £90m sale of our Sheffield Distribution Centre.’
Last week Debenhams Group sold its Sheffield distribution centre to Primark.
The group has been moving away from holding large amounts of its own stock and towards a marketplace model, where third-party brands sell through its platforms in exchange for a fee.
Fast-fashion firm Boohoo bought department store chain Debenhams out of administration in 2021, dispensing with its shops in a major blow to the High Street and switching online.
Finley has pledged to use the Debenhams brand, where Sex and the City star Kim Cattrall fronts a fashion campaign, as a ‘blueprint’ to transform the ailing fortunes of the wider group.
Last year, Debenhams said it was considering selling Manchester-based PrettyLittleThing.
But in January, it said it was ‘pleased with the pace and scale’ of a revival and ‘the resulting material improvement in profitability.’
WSG Brands owns fashion retailers including Von Dutch, whose apparel and caps were popular among Hollywood celebrities in the 2000s including Paris Hilton.

items.body:
Waitrose has launched a supermarket first, with own-brand fresh cows milk to sport a new on-pack ‘Championing Regenerative Farming’ logo highlighting the start of the regenerative farming journey which Waitrose dairy farmers are practising on their farms. All Waitrose fresh milk and cream is already 100% free-range, with Waitrose’s 40 British, dedicated dairy farm suppliers turning their cattle outside to graze for at least 183 days a year.
Charlotte Di Cello, chief commercial officer at Waitrose, comments: “We’re immensely proud to work with farmers who are taking proactive steps to farm with nature. The new Championing Regenerative Farming logo, which you can find on all Waitrose own-brand fresh milk, provides our customers with the reassurance that the farmers supplying their kitchen staples are staying one step ahead of the herd in protecting nature.”
Among those leading the charge is Stuart Rogers of Longmoor Farm in Dorset. As one of Waitrose’s dedicated dairy farmers, Stuart and his fellow farmers are taking active measures to restore natural systems, from growing cover crops to protect and regenerate living soil by locking in carbon and preventing water run-off, to planting trees directly in grazing fields (agroforestry) and actively measuring and improving baseline biodiversity.
Longmoor Farm went completely soya-free with their cow feed a decade ago, switching to homegrown maize planted without ploughing the ground (to minimise soil disturbance). Stuart has also established new hedgerows of willow, poplar, maple, and hazel to provide shelter and varied grazing for his Holstein cattle.
Stuart Rogers, Waitrose Dairy Farmer comments: “We’ve been doing a lot of this as a group for 20 years or so, but now it comes with more urgency. We are a nimble group, able and willing to take on challenges, especially as people learn it’s making their businesses more resilient.”
Recent Waitrose research shows that customers are linking premium food quality to farm-level sustainability. While 53% of under-45s and 58% of adults aged 45+ state they are most excited about food produced using nature-friendly farming methods.*
Waitrose’s updated own-brand fresh milk packaging, which will feature the new Championing Regenerative Farming logo, will be available on Waitrose shelves, and online from September.
* Waitrose research of 1,095 participants conducted 02.07.26-17.07/26

items.body:
Total Till sales at UK major supermarkets increased (+1.8%) in the four weeks ending 5th September 2026, according to the latest data released today by NielsenIQ (NIQ). This marked a slowdown from the average +3.2% growth recorded over the 12 weeks ending 8th August, as cooler weather and the return of back-to-school routines brought a reset in shopping behaviour following one of the hottest summers on record.
As the weather turned greyer, shoppers had less need for instant cooling refreshments and unit sales declined (-0.1%) during the period, the first time they have fallen since the four weeks ending 18th April 2026. Across all supermarkets and convenience stores, sales increased (+2.0%), with the strongest growth recorded over the August Bank Holiday weekend. Sales increased +3.1% in the week ending 29th August and peaked at £4.25bn.
There was also a shift in where shoppers chose to buy their groceries. Sales at larger sized supermarkets increased (+2.4%), while growth across convenience stores slowed (+0.3%) as consumers returned to more planned shopping trips following the summer holiday period.
Shoppers shift to comfort food and store cupboard staples
Although ice cream sales remained ahead of last year (+8.1%), sales fell (-22.6%) compared with the previous four weeks as temperatures cooled and households moved towards back-to-school routines. Other summer favourites also recorded sharp declines compared to the prior month, including olives (-16.4%), fresh dips (-10.4%) and fresh fruit (-6.9%).
At the same time, the changing of the seasons and return of school routines acting as a reset, helped more traditional comfort foods recover following the summer. Ambient grocery sales increased (+2.9%) in value versus a year ago, while unit growth returned to positive territory (+0.7%) after declining during the summer. This led to a significant growth in some store-cupboard staples. Sales of canned beans, excluding baked beans, increased (+10.1%) in the latest four weeks, driven in particular by butter beans, where value sales surged (+31.5%). Butter beans alone accounted for 58% of the value growth across the canned beans category.
There was also a marked growth in sales for gravy and stock, which increased +4.1% year on year and was 33.7% higher than the previous four-week period. Chilled soup (-3.7%) and ambient soup (-2.7%) remained in value decline year on year but both recorded double-digit sales growth compared with the previous four-week period, up +29.3% and +28.2% respectively. 1
The fading impact of the summer and FIFA World Cup was also evident across alcohol, with total alcohol value sales falling -0.4% compared with last year. Lager declined (-2.0%), alongside cider (-1.6%) and stout (-1.2%). However, pre-mixed alcoholic drinks continued to buck the trend, recording strong value growth (+24.7%). Soft drinks remained a standout performer, with shoppers spending £1.1bn and sales increasing +10.2% compared with last year. The category accounted for 32% of total store value growth during the period.
A focus on a September reset
As consumers move into autumn and become more selective about what they buy, health is also becoming an increasingly important consideration. Previous NIQ data shows that 12% of UK households now have a GLP-1 user, with the influence on eating habits extending beyond the individual using the medication. 2
This reflects a wider focus on healthier choices, 45% of UK shoppers saying they are eating more food from scratch, 37% eating more natural snacks, 31% checking food labels and avoiding specific additives, and 11% buying more organic products. 3 With this in mind, impulse products such as crisps, chocolate and soft drinks that state they are ‘all natural’ or made with ‘all natural ingredients’ grew (+9.4%) in the last four weeks, significantly ahead of the +5.4% growth recorded across the total impulse category. A similar trend can be seen in fresh food, where products labelled ‘organic’ grew +4.7%, compared with +1.9% for the overall fresh food category.4
Online channel grows
Over the latest 12 weeks, Ocado (+17.4%) and M&S (+10.8%) continued to lead grocery growth. M&S is driving larger baskets by targeting family shoppers, revitalising older stores with ‘destination’ food halls and expanding value-led ranges such as ‘Remarksable Value’ and ‘Bigger Pack, Better Value’. The strategy is paying off, with average basket value reaching £16.295 in the latest four weeks, up 9.1% year on year. Lidl also maintained strong sales momentum (+7.7%), followed by Waitrose (+2.6%).
Online grocery continued to outperform the wider market, with e-commerce sales up +10.1% in value with total sales of £2.1bn in the latest four weeks, up +0.9% on the previous month as consumers continue to reach for convenient delivery methods. 6
Mike Watkins, head of retailer and business insight at NielsenIQ, said: “Following one of the hottest summers on record, which encouraged consumers to spend more freely, September is likely to mark a return to tighter household budgeting. Currently, one in three households cite the cost of living as their biggest concern, while almost three-quarters expect to be moderately or severely impacted by financial pressures as we move into the autumn and winter months. With children now back at school, consumers are likely to enter a period of reassessing priorities, taking stock of finances, and monitoring spending more closely.”
Watkins continued: “Looking ahead, increased consumer scrutiny of spending creates the potential for greater price sensitivity and promotional intensity. As retailers enter the Golden Quarter, they will need to work harder and smarter to drive volume growth. This could involve encouraging shoppers to trade up through stronger mission-led propositions, leveraging personalisation to align with consumer values, and ensuring that festive marketing campaigns resonate with increasingly price-conscious consumers. By striking the right balance between value, relevance, and engagement, retailers can maximise opportunities during the critical run-up to Christmas.”

items.body:
Greggs, a leading UK food-on-the-go retailer, has opened its first supermarket ‘Bitesize Greggs’ within the Tesco Southwark Superstore.
The opening marks the latest step in the rollout of Greggs smaller shop format, which allows the company to bring a tailored range of its best-selling customer favourites, offering the same great quality and prices to customers in compact units in prime, high-footfall locations.
Open seven days a week, the ‘Bitesize Greggs’ at Tesco Southwark Superstore has created 10 new jobs for the local area. Located at 107 Dunston Road, Southwark, London, SE1 5HG, the shop provides customers convenient access to a selection of products including Sausage Rolls, Steak Bakes, Sweet Treats and Fairtrade hot drinks.
This latest store at Tesco Southwark Superstore follows the successful opening of ‘Bitesize Greggs’ locations at London Bridge Station, Sevenoaks Railway Station, Dartford Station and Cheshire Oaks Designer Outlet.
The more agile ‘Bitesize Greggs’ shop format alongside Greggs traditional, larger shops supports the company’s broader shop estate growth plans. In 2026, Greggs expects to open around 100–110 net new shops, and it continues to see a clear opportunity for at least 3,500 UK shops over the longer term, supported by investment in supply chain capacity required to enable that growth.
Tony Rowson, property director at Greggs, commented: “We’re delighted to announce the opening of our first ‘Bitesize Greggs’ within a supermarket at Tesco Southwark Superstore. Our Bitesize format allows us to bring Greggs to more customers from compact units in convenient, high-footfall locations, while still offering a selection of our best-selling products. This new opening is an exciting next step as part of our broader ambition to make Greggs even more accessible to customers across the UK.”
Liam Wagstaff, retail partnership manager at Tesco, said: “We’re always looking for ways to make the shopping trip even more convenient for our customers, and we’re pleased to welcome the first supermarket ‘Bitesize Greggs’ at our Southwark Superstore. Now customers can pick up all their Greggs favourites while popping in to do their weekly shop, offering even greater convenience.”

items.body:
Following today’s release of Wickes’ figures for the six months ending 27 June 2026; Jake Kendrick, Retail Analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers his view: “The soft performance in Wickes’ Retail division in H1 exposes the continued pressure in the core UK DIY market and the impact of wet weather on Q1 footfall. Wickes’s Retail revenue rose 0.8% for the first half of the financial year (-0.3% LFL), and within this, TradePro sales increased 5% year-on-year (and TradePro active members 9%), signalling a poor performance in DIY. Shares rose in early trading as Wickes affirmed it remained on track for 10% adjusted PBT growth for the full year, supported by stronger Q3 retail trading to date and lower business rates.
“The specialist’s Design & Installation (D&I) proposition proved resilient in H1, with revenue increasing 5.7% – revenue is recognised once installation is complete so is not immediately tied to Retail sales performance. Growth in D&I was supported by Lifestyle Kitchens and Bespoke Bathrooms. However, softer Bespoke Kitchen orders pointed to continued consumer caution around higher-ticket projects.
“Competitive pressure within the trade audience is intensifying, with Screwfix reporting continued growth in trade customers and further market-share gains. Wickes will have to defend its trade advantage in H2 by reinforcing its service and product differentiation through tailored trade support and sharpening TradePro promotions.
“Wickes needs to rebuild its engagement with DIY shoppers so it is less reliant on trade. Investments in digital design, rapid fulfilment and AI will make home improvement easier and more convenient for consumers. Still, Wickes can go further by helping customers complete projects, not just buy products. Ofgem’s 13% energy price cap increase from July 2026, driven by higher wholesale gas prices linked to the Middle East conflict, creates a clear customer need for energy-saving solutions. Wickes should leverage the newly legal plug-in solar panels and its specialist advice to introduce customers to home-energy upgrades, with the potential to convert consumers into larger Wickes Solar installations. This approach turns pressure on household budgets into a growth opportunity, differentiating the retailer through expertise rather than price alone.”

items.title: Asda hails 'important milestone' as sales rise for the first time in more than two years
items.summary: Britain's third biggest supermarket saw sales increase 0.1 per cent to £4.17 billion in the 12 weeks to 6 September - the first time they have grown since March 2024.
items.body:
Asda hails 'important milestone' as sales rise for the first time in more than two years
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Asda hailed an ‘important milestone' after reporting quarterly sales growth for the first time in more than two years after struggling under private equity ownership.
Britain’s third biggest supermarket saw sales increase 0.1 per cent to £4.17billion in the 12 weeks to September 6 – the first time they have grown since March 2024.
Asda has battled falling sales since TDR Capital helped to finance a debt-fuelled £6.8billion takeover by the billionaire Issa brothers in 2021.
It has since lost out to discounters Lidl and Aldi, and grappled with debt pressures and severe disruption linked to an IT upgrade.
The figures come just weeks after boss Allan Leighton said it was 'about a third' of the way through its recovery, which has seen the supermarket slash prices and upgrade its online operations.
But new figures show Asda's market share fell to 11.5 per cent, from 11.8 per cent a year ago. Researchers at Worldpanel said the Leeds-based grocer had retained a higher share of 16 per cent in the North of England.
Revival: Asda boss Allan Leighton has been attempting to reverse the struggling grocer's fortunes
They also said it is outperforming the market in categories including hot drinks, ice cream and chilled poultry.
An Asda spokesperson said: ‘Asda returning to growth for the first time in more than two years is an important milestone. The investments we have made to strengthen our proposition, lower prices and improve the shopping experience are clearly resonating with customers.
‘At the same time, we remain in the foothills of recovery with more to do as we look to build a stronger Asda for the long term.’
Last month, Leighton hailed signs of a revival after sales rose 0.2 per cent over the seven weeks to August 18. This snapshot was a return to growth for the first time in more than two years.
But Asda said sales fell 2.3 per cent for the three months to the end of June, with revenue of £5.1billion.
Earlier this year, Asda accounts revealed that pre-tax losses had widened from £599million in 2024 to £989million in 2025, as total sales fell 3.4 per cent to £25.9billion.
Leighton, who rejoined the Leeds-based retailer in November 2024, has warned that his revival plan will not be an overnight fix and slashing prices will hit profits.
But he warned there was pressure on prices due to the heatwave affecting crops this summer.
'The crops are in a tricky state, not just in the UK, everywhere, you know clearly and it's more a produce issue than anything else.'
He said that the grocer had thousands of producers and growers and is 'working very hard with them' to ensure availability 'sticks up as well as we can' and to 'manage the inflation in the best way we can'.
'We generally inflate below the market anyway, so generally when there's high inflation, that's quite a good thing for us.'
He added: 'But the biggest thing is consumer sentiment. How do people feel? Do they feel as if they want to spend? Do they have the money to spend? That's always been the driver of it.'
Britain’s number one and two supermarkets Tesco and Sainsbury’s saw sales rise 1.7 per cent and 2.9 per cent respectively.
Lidl saw its sales surge by 8 per cent - the biggest leap out of all the physical grocers. It has been pumping cash into opening more shops across the country. Its market share increased to 8.7 per cent, compared to 8.3 per cent a year ago.
Marks & Spencer also saw its grocery sales leap by 14.8 per cent after the retailer has invested in refurbishments and opening glossier shops. Worldpanel does not include market share for M&S as it also sells clothes.
And online grocer Ocado saw sales up 13.3 per cent and was the fastest growing grocer overall for the 30th time in a row.

items.title: Dueling Amazon, Target October sales events return
items.summary: With the holidays right around the corner, both retailers will hold deal days next month on everything from toys to groceries and apparel.
items.body:
Dive Brief:
- Target and Amazon’s dueling October sale events return next month, according to company press releases Tuesday. Both companies will promote deals from Oct. 6 to Oct. 7.
- Amazon’s Big Deal Days sale for paid Prime members features discounts spanning fragrances from Phlur, Shark appliances, select groceries and more, with new drops both days. Ahead of the holidays, toy brand FAO Schwarz also has a new Amazon storefront, and Amazon created holiday gift lists for shoppers.
- The Target Circle Deal Days event is open to members of its free loyalty program, though customers paying for the Target Circle 360 membership will get access a day early. The event features deals on clothing, toys, holiday decor and more.
Dive Insight:
The leaves are just starting to fall in parts of the U.S., meaning it's that time of year again when major retailers — like Target and Walmart — often compete with e-commerce giant Amazon during sales events.
“Once fall arrives, there's so much to get ready for — the hosting, the decorating, the holiday gifting — and Prime Big Deal Days makes it easy to check it all off while saving," Carmen Nestares, Amazon’s vice president of North America marketing and Prime tech, said in a statement.
The return of the holiday season comes at a pivotal point for Target. The retailer has seen some progress on its broader turnaround effort in the recent fiscal quarters and is working to avoid the sales drop it saw in Q4 last year.
Target’s Q2 net sales increased 5.3% year over year to $26.5 billion, with sales in all core merchandising categories growing. However, the apparel and home categories saw lower rates of improvement during the period.
Target’s announcement for next month’s Circle Deals Day event highlights deals on many of its private label brands, such as kids clothing label Cat & Jack and furniture brand Threshold.
Amazon held its annual Prime Day sales event in June, marking a slightly earlier run from its usual July dates. The e-commerce company did not release its usual post-event press release following Prime Day this year, which typically outlines some of the best-selling products.
The company’s Q2 online store net sales grew 15% year over year to about $70.4 billion and physical store net sales grew 4% to reach nearly $5.8 billion.

items.title: New wave of mortgage rate rises as five high street banks make chunky home loan hikes on the same day
items.summary: The housing market is enduring another wave of mortgage rates hikes this week ahead of the Bank of England's next interest rate decision on Thursday.
items.body:
New wave of mortgage rate rises as five high street banks make chunky home loan hikes on the same day
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Britain's biggest banks announced a wave of mortgage rate hikes today ahead of the Bank of England's next interest rate decision on Thursday.
Major lenders including NatWest, Santander, HSBC, Lloyds Bank and TSB all announced increases within hours of each other in a blow for homeowners, as concern grows over the future direction of inflation and interest rates.
Experts now think there could be five rises in the base rate between now and the end of next year.
Santander, in particular, has announced chunky rises. From tomorrow it will be increasing two-year fixes by up to 0.45 percentage points and raising five-year fixes by up to 0.4 percentage points.
Aaron Strutt, of mortgage broker Trinity Financial, said: 'I can't remember the last time five of the big six lenders hiked their rates on the same day.
'These Santander rates are going to come as a bit of a shock to customers who check today and again on Wednesday.
'It looks like this Santander rate change means the bank is pulling the last of its sub-5 per cent rates. Santander had a 4.52 per cent two-year fix a few days ago.'
Major banks, including NatWest, Santander, HSBC, Lloyds Bank and TSB, all increased mortgage rates this week for the second time since the start of September
Elsewhere, Barclays' market-leading 4.55 per cent two-year fix with an £899 product fee will rise to 4.75 per cent.
The bank only increased its fixed rates a few days ago.
HSBC's lowest two-year fix is now 4.79 per cent and its cheapest five-year fix is 4.75 per cent.
Strutt added: 'It looks like Barclays has raised lots of its deals to over 5 per cent, which is something we were hoping would not happen despite all the economic tensions.
'HSBC's changes seem pretty reasonable compared to some of the other lenders. Its Premier customer rates are marginally cheaper.'
Alongside the five high street banks, several building societies have also started to reprice for the second time this week, including Nationwide, which increased selected fixed rates by as much as 0.3 percentage points this week.
Since the beginning of March, the average two-year fixed mortgage rate has risen by 0.89 percentage points, according to money comparison website Moneyfacts.
On a £250,000 mortgage being repaid over 25 years, Moneyfacts says this will have typically added £131 to monthly repayments, or £1,572 per year.
The Bank of England has estimated there are 750,000 households with a fixed rate of below 3 per cent that are set to expire in 2026.
Many of these households will be on rates between 1 and 2 per cent and could be facing the prospect of fixing at around 5 per cent now.
A homeowner with a £250,000 mortgage on a 25-year repayment term locking in at 5 per cent could expect to pay £1,462 a month.
That's £462 more a month than they would be paying if their rate was 1.5 per cent.
Worryingly, the situation for homeowners could get worse before it gets better, due to a recent spike in Sonia swap rates – which reflect market interest rate expectations.
Mortgage lenders enter into these swap agreements with other financial institutions to shield themselves against the interest rate risk involved with lending fixed rate mortgages.
Sonia swap rates are influenced by long-term market projections for the Bank of England base rate, as well as the wider economy, internal bank targets and competitor pricing.
Put simply, they create a benchmark of where the market thinks interest rates will go – though they can shift quickly in light of economic changes.
The problem is, when Sonia swap rates go up, the cost of borrowing increases for lenders, which is then passed to homeowners in the form of higher mortgage rates.
Today, five-year swaps hit 4.78 per cent, up from 4.28 per cent a month ago. Meanwhile two-year swaps were at 4.7 per cent, up from 4.17 per cent.
Sonia swaps are becoming more common due to market fears over the impact of rising oil prices on future inflation and interest rates.
Due to this spike in Sonia swaps, it is 'highly likely' other lenders will follow suit and adjust their rates, according to Rachel Springall, finance expert at Moneyfacts.
She said: 'The mortgage pain shows no sign of easing for those borrowers who cannot yet lock into a new deal, particularly those with a five-year fixed who are not due to refinance until 2027.
'Back in February 2022, there were sub-2 per cent fixed mortgages available, so moving off this rate will be a huge shock for borrowers.'
Santander has announced that from tomorrow it will be increasing two-year fixes by 0.45 percentage points and a 0.4 percentage point hike on five-year fixes
Will the Bank of England increase interest rates?
The Bank of England has refrained from any rate hikes since December last year, holding the base rate at 3.75 per cent for five consecutive meetings.
At its last vote on July 30, seven members of the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee voted for a hold, while two wanted to increase the base rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4 per cent.
At present, most economists expect another hold this week, and a rise of 0.25 per cent in November.
There is also speculation that four out of the five policy decisions between February and July 2027 will see base rate hikes.
The total cumulative increase of five rises would add 1.25 per cent to base rate.
Springall thinks there is every chance of a surprise interest rate hike this week.
She said: 'This will be hugely disappointing news for borrowers. It demonstrates how fixed mortgage rates are not intrinsically linked to adjustments to the Bank of England base rate, yet mortgage rates could climb even higher if the MPC decide to increase the base rate.
'If there is a spread vote between the doves and hawks, the Bank of England Governor, Andrew Bailey, will cast the deciding vote.'

RH Amar will distribute 11 SKUs from the ‘Knoops At Home’… This story continues at Knoops appoints RH Amar to accelerate ‘Knoops At Home’ range growth Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
RH Amar will distribute 11 SKUs from the ‘Knoops At Home’ range of hand-flaked drinking chocolate including the signature 54% House Blend and hugely popular 43% Single Origin Venezuela.
The partnership marks the first time Knoops has appointed a dedicated UK distributor, with RH Amar’s remit including grocery, speciality, wholesale, foodservice and online, helping to extend the reach of Knoops’ retail offering beyond its own stores, knoops.com and other existing retail channels.
Last year, Knoops invested in ‘The Flakery’ – its new production and warehousing facility to support the continued growth of its luxury drinking chocolate across both its store estate and ‘Knoops At Home’ range.
Jo Brett, COO of Knoops, said: “We’re excited to partner with RH Amar to bring our ‘Knoops At Home’ range of hand-flaked chocolate to more customers across the UK.
“RH Amar’s expertise and extensive network of specialist retailers and distribution channels will help us accelerate our UK growth, build greater awareness and access to the Knoops brand, and meet the strong demand we’re already seeing across our existing sales channels.”
Justin Burbage, commercial director at RH Amar, said: “Knoops is a fantastic addition to our portfolio and comes at an exciting time for the premium drinks category, as consumers continue to seek high-quality, indulgent products to enjoy at home.
“We are looking forward to building on the success of this exciting brand beyond its own stores and unlocking new opportunities for the ‘Knoops At Home’ range.”
Founded in 2013 by master chocolate sommelier Jens Knoop, Knoops has grown from a single store in Rye, East Sussex, to an international chocolate drinks brand with more than 30 stores in the UK and overseas.
Knoops will join RH Amar’s portfolio of brands including Mutti, Dunkin, Bold Bean, Weetabix, Kikkoman and Del Monte. It is a third-generation family-run business, and this year achieved B Corp accreditation.

items.title: Co-op and Southern Co-op merger faces CMA obstacle
items.summary: During the phase 1 investigation int the merger between the Co-op Group and Southern Co-op, the CMA has decided, on the evidence currently available to it, that it may be expected to result in a substantial lessening of competition within a market or markets in… This story continues at Co-op and Southern Co-op merger faces CMA obstacle Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
This is as a result of horizontal unilateral effects in the retail supply of groceries in convenience stores in local areas centring around nine CGL convenience stores and 10 Southern convenience stores, and the supply of attended at-need and pre-paid funeral services in local areas centring around one CGL site and one Southern site.
As a result of these concerns, the parties have until 22 September 2026 to offer UILs (undertakings in lieu – formal, binding promises offered by companies to a competition authority) which might be accepted by the CMA to address the competition concerns.
If no such UILs are offered, or the CMA decides that any UILs offered are insufficient to remedy its concerns, then the CMA will refer the merger for an in-depth phase 2 investigation.
A spokesperson for the Co-op Group said: “We welcome the update from the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), regarding its Phase 1 review of the proposed Southern Co-op transaction.
“We are pleased that, as anticipated, the CMA hasn’t identified competition concerns at a national level. It has identified a small number of locations where there is both a Southern and Co-op Group presence and where they believe there may be an adverse impact on competition for consumers. We will continue to engage and work with the CMA on the proposed remedies.
“There are no changes for colleagues, members or customers at this stage.

items.body:
For AW26, Tu presents a confident womenswear collection bringing together wardrobe-building essentials, directional trend pieces and an emphasis on quality and craftsmanship. Designed to mix seamlessly into modern wardrobes, the collection plays with rich texture, bold colour and contemporary silhouettes, bringing a more elevated point of view to everyday dressing. The range also keeps value front and centre, with 86% of AW26 womenswear priced under £30 and 65% under £25.
AW26 lands in phased monthly drops from September through to December, with each edit introducing a distinct seasonal story. September opens with warm neutrals, pops of orange and rich brown tones; October introduces green hues and frogging-detail alongside the season’s peak coat launch; and November moves into red, statement florals and decorative embellishment, bringing a more occasion-ready feel to versatile pieces for the festive season ahead.
Premium fabrics take centre stage
Following the success of Tu’s sold-out 2025 100% cashmere launch and this summer’s standout 100% linen edit, AW26 builds on growing demand for quality pieces at accessible prices. Knitwear is a particular focus, with an expanded range spanning merino, lambswool, cashmere, mohair and alpaca. The result is a collection of versatile wardrobe staples that combine premium fabrics, contemporary design and accessible value, designed to be worn and loved year after year.
Colour, texture and everyday expression define the season
AW26 embraces a more polished approach to day-to-day styling, with sharper silhouettes, funnel necklines, sculpted layering and fluid draping introducing shape and movement throughout. Lustrous satins, soft velvets, sheer finishes and subtle embellishment bring richness and tactility to looks that transition effortlessly from day to evening.
Standout pieces include the Burgundy Check Kilt (£28), Mono Faux Fur Jacket (£45), Brown Sequin Lace Camisole (£22.50), Mid Denim Embellished Jean (£35) and Cheetah Leather Pony Skin Shopper (£45), capturing the collection’s confident, expressive mood while responding to demand for versatile pieces that move effortlessly through every part of the season.
Outerwear steps up a gear
Outerwear takes centre stage this season, from wool-blend coats and faux fur-lined parkas to military-inspired detailing, funnel necks and oversized down puffers. The range balances fashion-forward design with everyday versatility, spanning statement silhouettes and timeless investment pieces.
Highlights include the Denim Military Jacket (£30), Double-Faced Wool Blend Coat (£85) and Tu’s first down-filled puffer coat (£85), made with recycled down and feathers. A fully waterproof parka (£55) also joins the collection, adding a functional, all-weather option.
Accessories and footwear complete the look
That same confidence extends to accessories and footwear, with suede, leather and pony-hair bringing defined finishes and contemporary design to the collection. The Zebra Leather Ponyskin Slouch Handheld Bag (£30) makes a statement, while the Brown Faux Fur Pillbox Hat (£12) and Faux Fur Clutch with Gold Handle (£18) tap into the season’s playful retro influence.
Footwear sees some of autumn’s biggest trends, with ruched boots, wedge heels and almond-toe shapes alongside the continued return of ballet flats and leopard print. The Black Suede Ruched Mid-Height Boot (£50) is a key style, combining gathered detailing with an easy mid-height shape, while padded footbeds feature across selected styles for added comfort.
Mel Evans, head of womenswear buying, says: “This season is a real step forward for Tu womenswear. We’ve put a lot of focus into fabric, fit and design detail, creating pieces that feel special while still delivering the value our customers expect from us. What I love about AW26 is that it gives customers more choice across every part of their wardrobe, from cashmere, lambswool and mohair knitwear to standout coats, accessories and easy everyday pieces. Customers don’t have to choose between style, quality and value. This collection brings all three together in a way that feels modern, wearable and
accessible. My personal favourite is the Double-Faced Wool Blend Coat. It has that polished, premium feel, but it’s still incredibly versatile and easy to wear.”
The AW26 womenswear collection launches in phased drops from September through to December, available online at tu.co.uk and argos.co.uk, and in selected Sainsbury’s stores nationwide. Prices start from £5, with womenswear available in UK sizes 6-26 and XS-XL and footwear in UK sizes 3-8.

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. We think carefully about the mattress we sleep on, the chair we sit in and even the pillow we rest our head on. Clarks is challenging consumers to reconsider what’s on their feet by asking people across […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch!
