items.body:
We think carefully about the mattress we sleep on, the chair we sit in and even the pillow we rest our head on. But how much thought do we give to the shoes carrying us through thousands of steps every day?
Clarks is challenging consumers to reconsider what’s on their feet by asking people across the nation, ‘Are You Wearing The Right Shoes?’ in a bold new campaign designed to provoke conversation around everyday comfort and whether we’re making the right choices when it comes to our footwear.
Rolling out across TikTok, social media, OOH, retail and digital environments, the campaign brings the idea to life through a series of unexpected, humorous and deliberately uncomfortable scenarios.
From shoppers rushing to the nearest chair to rest their tired feet, to animated dogs gathering at a humorous C360 FoamTM support group to complain about just how far their owners now want to walk, the campaign takes a playful approach to a familiar problem.
At the centre of the campaign is C360 FoamTM, Clarks’ most advanced proprietary comfort technology, first introduced in 2025 through Clarks Pace Walk, the brand’s first performance walking shoe.
Engineered with dual-layer cushioning to absorb impact, return energy and support natural walking movement, C360 FoamTM helps wearers walk further for longer, while delivering exceptional cushioning and comfort.
Now, Clarks is taking that technology somewhere new…
INTRODUCING CLARKS CODE: performance technology meets everyday style
This Autumn, Clarks is taking C360 FoamTM beyond performance walking and into everyday footwear for the first time with the launch of Clarks Code. The new collection answers a simple
question: why should performance-led comfort only exist in performance shoes?
Style-led, but comfort-driven
Designed to move with consumers throughout the day and across different occasions, Code brings C360 FoamTM technology to a growing range of men’s and women’s silhouettes – without compromising on style.
Think a contemporary loafer with built-in comfort for the morning commute and office, or a sleek white leather trainer that works just as well for dinner as it does for a laid-back weekend.
Certified podiatrist and foot surgeon, Clarks brand ambassador Dr Sarah Haller said: “Our feet carry us through our entire day, yet footwear is often chosen around style or occasion, with comfort becoming a secondary consideration.
What I find exciting about Clarks Code is that you don’t have to make that choice. It brings together styles you’ll genuinely want to wear with exceptional built-in comfort for every step.”
Comfort without the compromise
Advanced comfort technology doesn’t have to come with an inaccessible price tag.
With prices starting from just £89 / $110 / €99.95, Clarks Code brings together contemporary style and advanced comfort technology at an accessible price point.
Available now at Clarks.com, Clarks retail stores and selected wholesale partners.

Products […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Bedkingdom, a furniture e-commerce retailer headquartered in Liversedge, West Yorkshire has launched the brand in Ireland.
The Irish website will stock 90% of Bedkingdom’s own-brand range of bedroom and home furniture products, and customers in the country will be able to shop without added duties and taxes, with free delivery on orders above €250.00.
Products will initially be shipped from the UK, while the brand establishes itself in Ireland. In the future, the team plans to expand operations and open a warehouse in the country to simplify shipping and facilitate next day delivery options.
Bedkingdom has been working on this expansion for the past six months, and the Irish website launched in early September. It comes after the UK brand goes from strength to strength, following 54% year-on-year organic traffic growth and continued commercial success.
Chief Operating Officer, Levon Hall comments, “When we started looking at where to launch the business next, Ireland was the obvious choice because of its close proximity to the UK. We’ve done a lot of research, and Irish people tend to take a lot of pride in their homes, with a big culture of hospitality and bringing family together, which made it the perfect fit.
“There’s been a lot of hoops to jump through with preparing to enter a completely new market, especially post Brexit which has added a layer of complication for retailers that want to ship products outside the UK.
“As well as our owned brands, we stock several ranges from other furniture manufacturers and suppliers, and hope to establish some partnerships with new suppliers that want to access the Irish market.”
Bedkingdom’s founder, Ashley Hainsworth, began selling mattresses online with an investment of £400 while studying at Huddersfield University, and now has three West Yorkshire warehouses and £28m+ revenue across the Flair Furniture Group. In 2023, it was listed in the Sunday Times Top 100 after achieving 76.06% average annual sales growth over three years, and placed 18th in the Ward Hadaway Yorkshire Fastest 50 in 2025.
Bedkingdom has several brand-owned ranges of furniture, including Flair Beds, Flair Furnishings, Noomi, Recoil Gaming, and SOLACE+CO, and curates a collection of boutique furniture brands from third-party suppliers.

items.title: Retail jobs fall as employment costs soar, ONS figures show
items.summary: According to the latest ONS figures, there were 2.75 million retail jobs in June 2026. Using the four-quarter average which smooths out the seasonal variations in hiring, there was 2.78 million jobs in retail in the year-to-Q2 2026, 62,000 fewer than a year earlier, 122,000… This story continues at Retail jobs fall as employment costs soar, ONS figures show Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Using the four-quarter average which smooths out the seasonal variations in hiring, there was 2.78 million jobs in retail in the year-to-Q2 2026, 62,000 fewer than a year earlier, 122,000 fewer than two years ago, and 410,000 fewer than a decade ago.
This four-quarter average is the lowest on record.
Using the four-quarter average, there were 1.29 million full-time and 1.50 million part-time jobs. The number of part-time retail jobs is the lowest on record.
Retail remains the largest private sector employer in the UK, bigger than both hospitality, at 2.62 million, and manufacturing, at 2.35 million.
The 2024 Budget changes to the National Insurance contributions (NICs) threshold and rate, which came into effect in April 2025, cost retailers £2.3bn. Combined with two above-inflation annual rises in the National Living Wage, retailers’ employment costs have spiralled by £6.5bn in just two years.
Commenting on these figures, Helen Dickinson, chief executive, British Retail Consortium, said:
“Entry-level retail jobs are vanishing at the very moment they are needed most. With one in seven young people now not in education, employment or training, the loss of 122,000 jobs in the last two years means tens of thousands fewer opportunities for young people to get their first step on the career ladder, build skills and earn a living.
“These job losses have not happened by accident. Retailers are being hit by a tidal wave of employment costs.
“In just two years, increases to National Insurance Contributions and the National Living Wage have added £6.5bn in costs, while further employment reforms risk making it even harder to create and sustain jobs.
“Retailers are going above and beyond to help young people and tackle the UK NEETs crisis. Through our new initiative ‘Opening Shift’, retailers have already pledged over 11,000 work experience places, with many more to come. The industry aims to create 100,000 job opportunities for young people, but government must match that ambition with policies that support job creation, not make it harder.
“Raising the NICs threshold to £6,000, which would help retailers invest, hire and give thousands more young people that vital first step on the jobs ladder.”

items.title: Yoti and partners to help shops accept digital proof of age for alcohol sales
items.summary: Digital identity company Yoti, has announced partnerships with leading technology providers to help UK retailers introduce digital age checks for alcohol sales. The development follows a change in the law allowing Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID, as well as other digital IDs certified to… This story continues at Yoti and partners to help shops accept digital proof of age for alcohol sales Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The development follows a change in the law allowing Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID, as well as other digital IDs certified to the UK government’s Digital Verification Services (DVS) Trust Framework, to be used as proof of age when buying alcohol in licensed premises.
For retailers and other licensed businesses, this offers another way to complete age checks, while giving customers more choice in how they prove their age.
Diebold Nixdorf, Flooid, StrongPoint, Kestronics and Zebra Technologies provide point of sale and self-checkout technology to the UK’s leading supermarkets, retail and hospitality businesses.
Through their partnerships with Yoti, the technology partners and retailers will integrate digital ID checks into their existing point of sale and self-checkout systems, making it easier for licensed businesses already using their technology to begin accepting digital proof of age.
For smaller independent retailers and licensed premises, Yoti has a free ID Checker mobile and web app and a partnership with Licensing Connect.
The app allows staff to quickly and securely check that a customer’s digital proof of age is authentic and valid.
More than 15,000 businesses downloaded the ID Checker app ahead of the change in law, meaning many premises can start accepting Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID for alcohol sales from today.
Customers will no longer have to rely on carrying a passport or driving licence to prove their age to buy alcohol. Instead, customers can use the free Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID apps. Together, the apps have been downloaded by over 8 million people in the UK, with 170,000 new downloads a month.
Around 25% of 18-24 year olds have downloaded the apps. Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID allow people to share only the information needed for an age check, for example, that they’re over 18.
This means they can prove their age without revealing additional personal information that may be on a physical ID, such as their full name, exact date of birth or address.
“Digital proof of age has the potential to make age-restricted purchases simpler, faster and more convenient for everyone involved,” said Matt Redwood, vice president, solutions & consulting group at Diebold Nixdorf.
“For guests and shoppers, it means a smoother checkout experience with greater choice and privacy. For retailers, it can improve throughput, reduce manual interventions and support more efficient store operations.
“And for store colleagues, it creates a clearer and more consistent age verification process, helping reduce friction at the point of sale and enabling more positive customer engagement.”
“For retailers and hospitality businesses, digital proof of age offers a practical new option for managing age-restricted sales at the point of service,” said Mark Shirran, managing director of Kestronics.
“It can help make checks quicker and more consistent for colleagues, while giving customers a more convenient way to prove they are over 18.”
Until now, the Mandatory Licensing Conditions under the Licensing Act 2003 required acceptable proof of age for alcohol sales to contain physical security features, such as a hologram or ultraviolet mark, preventing digital IDs from being used for these checks.
The change in law now allows licensed premises in England and Wales to use digital IDs certified to the UK government’s DVS Trust Framework.
Digital ID will be an additional choice, rather than replacing physical documents or requiring every business to accept digital ID.
Only digital ID apps certified against the DVS Trust Framework will be accepted under the new legislative changes. Both the Yoti and Post Office EasyID apps already meet these requirements.
Robin Tombs, chief executive, Yoti said: “The change in law to allow digital IDs for alcohol sales is a landmark moment for digital identity in the UK.
“We’ve been working towards this moment since Yoti was founded in 2014 and we’re delighted to work with leading technology providers including Diebold Nixdorf, Flooid, StrongPoint, Kestronics and Zebra Technologies to make it simple for businesses to start accepting digital proof of age.”

items.title: Parents seek out school uniform deals, cutting average spend to £54.53
items.summary: Overall grocery inflation jumps to 2.3%, as Ocado and Lidl gain market share Business live – latest updates Parents and carers spent 12.5% less on school uniform in the run-up to the start of this academic year, turning to promotions and second-hand items to keep expenses down as families struggled with the cost of living crisis . The average spend on school uniform was £54.53 in the four weeks to 6 September, down an eighth from £62.29 in the same period last year, according to the market research company Worldpanel by Numerator. Overall grocery inflation picked up to 2.3% from 2.1%. Continue reading...
items.body:
Parents and carers spent 12.5% less on school uniform in the run-up to the start of this academic year, turning to promotions and second-hand items to keep expenses down as families struggled with the cost of living crisis.
The average spend on school uniform was £54.53 in the four weeks to 6 September, down an eighth from £62.29 in the same period last year, according to the market research company Worldpanel by Numerator. Overall grocery inflation picked up to 2.3% from 2.1%.
Fraser McKevitt, the head of retail and consumer insight at the company, said “value is the watchword for parents this back-to-school season” as they try to balance stretched household budgets.
Almost half of households (44%) prioritised keeping costs low above all else when it comes to buying uniform, even if that means compromising on quality, while a third (33%) aimed to strike a balance between the two, according to a back to school survey conducted by Worldpanel in August.
“It’s a clear sign that, for many families, the return to school is landing at a difficult time financially, and retailers who can offer reassurance on price without compromising on quality stand will stand in good stead,” McKevitt said.
Grocery sales rose 2% year on year over the period, the monthly Worldpanel figures showed. August brought more warm weather and the end of a summer of sport. But with the return to school and work looming for many, shopping habits began to shift. Shoppers made 18m fewer trips to supermarkets compared with a peak of 497m in July.
“The end of the summer holidays typically brings a cooling in trip frequency and a pivot towards priority purchases, and this year is no exception,” McKevitt said. “While grocery inflation ticked up modestly last month, it remains significantly lower than the levels we saw earlier in the year, giving households some welcome breathing room.”
Sandwiches featured in more than half of all kids’ lunchboxes, with more than half a million more households that include children buying loaves of bread in the seven days to 6 September compared with the previous week. The number buying satsumas (+29%) and cucumbers (+21%) also rose in the final week before the return to school.
Sales at Asda rose by 0.1% over the 12 weeks to 6 September, as the grocer returned to growth for the first time since March 2024. However, the Leeds-based retailer’s market share dipped to 11.5%.
The online supermarket Ocado, with sales up by 13.3%, remained the fastest-growing grocer overall, with a slightly higher market share of 2.2%. Lidl moved up to 8.7% of the market.
Sainsbury’s and Morrisons maintained their previous market share of 15.2% and 8.4%, respectively. The UK’s largest supermarket, Tesco, dipped to 27.8% from 28.1%. The German discounter Aldi took a 10.6% share.

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Scandit, the leader in smart data capture, today announced Self-Checkout Loss Prevention, a real-time vision AI solution that helps retailers detect loss patterns (whether accidental or intentional) as they happen. The solution empowers shoppers to self-correct, without store associate intervention in the majority of cases, to keep the checkout flow uninterrupted. Scandit’s entry into the loss […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Scandit, the leader in smart data capture, today announced Self-Checkout Loss Prevention, a real-time vision AI solution that helps retailers detect loss patterns (whether accidental or intentional) as they happen. The solution empowers shoppers to self-correct, without store associate intervention in the majority of cases, to keep the checkout flow uninterrupted.
Scandit’s entry into the loss prevention market addresses one of retail’s most visible tensions: reducing loss at self checkout without adding friction that frustrates shoppers or burdens store teams. Self-checkout now handles 54% of transactions in stores that have it. Those stores carry losses 33% higher than comparable stores without it, and loss rises an average of 22% in the year after installation, according to ECR Retail Loss’s Self-Checkout Loss Report 2026. Random spot checks can take in excess of two minutes, according to one German retailer causing customer friction and absorbing associate time.
With Self-Checkout Loss Prevention, a soft on-screen nudge to shoppers, or attendant notification if escalated, corrects any flagged items before a transaction is completed, resulting in the recovery or deterrence of more than 75% of losses attributed to self-checkout. This includes known loss patterns such as missed scans, intentionally skipped items, left in trolley and abandoned transactions.
“Self-checkout fundamentally changed retail, but it also changed the loss equation,” said Christian Floerkemeier, Scandit CTO and co-founder. “Retailers shouldn’t have to choose between a fast checkout experience and strong loss prevention. Self-Checkout Loss Prevention gives them a software-first way to detect issues in real time, with the process configurable to a retailer’s own policy. In addition to recovering losses, it also enables retailers to optimise labour usage more productively.”
Self-Checkout loss prevention deploys as a per-station architecture, which eliminates the need for dedicated servers and complex installation, while unlocking a scalable deployment from small store formats to large hypermarkets. The hardware-agnostic solution works with existing camera infrastructure – whether built-in, off-the-shelf, or standard security cameras above the self-checkout station – eliminating the need for purpose-built AI hardware, to maintain a low total cost of ownership.
With privacy at its core, the solution processes video on the station and is designed to support retailers in meeting GDPR obligations. Analysing items and transaction activity only means no facial or biometric identification is required, avoiding by design the practices the EU AI Act prohibits, and is all backed by Scandit’s ISO 27001 certification.
“One of the challenges of vision AI checks at self-checkout has been the heavy infrastructure cost and latency involved in some legacy solutions which often created a disconnect between the behaviour and the timing of the intervention, leading to confusion for all involved,” commented Greg Buzek, president and principal analyst, IHL Group. “A lightweight solution that is easy to deploy in stores removes that cost and latency, and where existing cameras can be reused, lowers the cost further. That can be a win-win for retailers: deterring deliberate theft while quickly resolving the honest mistakes that would otherwise slow the transaction process.”
With this announcement and Scandit’s launch of Age Verified Self-Checkout in July 2026, the two biggest friction points which require associate involvement are significantly reduced. Age-Verified Self-Checkout enables retailers to automate and verify self-checkout purchases of age-restricted items to reduce lane delays, remove avoidable associate intervention and improve compliance. With both solutions combined, Scandit provides a more autonomous self-checkout model that supports age-verification compliance, protected on loss, and frees up associates for higher value work instead of routine checks.
These announcements build on Scandit’s broader vision for store intelligence and is the latest expansion of its retail solutions portfolio also encompassing on-shelf availability via ShelfView, price and planogram compliance, expiry date management and markdown and intelligent in-store picking. Retailers can turn store data into real-time inventory visibility and prioritise actions to protect profit and reduce operational risk.

items.title: Wickes gains as Brits go budget in kitchen refurbs
items.summary: Wickes is benefiting from a slowdown in consumer spending as Brits switch to the value home improvement retailer and away from premium rivals, its boss has said. The FTSE 250 group posted a 2.1 per cent jump in revenue to £865m in the six months to June, buoyed by rising sales of big ticket items [...]
items.body:
Wickes gains as Brits go budget in kitchen refurbs
Wickes is benefiting from a slowdown in consumer spending as Brits switch to the value home improvement retailer and away from premium rivals, its boss has said.
The FTSE 250 group posted a 2.1 per cent jump in revenue to £865m in the six months to June, buoyed by rising sales of big ticket items like bathrooms and kitchens.
David Wood, the retailer’s chief executive, said Wickes is attracting more customers and transactions despite fragile consumer confidence and a slowdown in demand for new homes.
The home improvement boss told City AM that Wickes’ customers are choosing “more affordable” cabinets while still opting for premium ovens, microwaves and work surfaces.
“There is some thoughtfulness and consideration from the customer, because the average order value is lower than previous years as customers do cut their cloth accordingly,” he said.
Wood said consumers are not stalling home refurbishments altogether: “For the last half a decade in the market, kitchen and bathroom volumes actually have been down, so those kitchens and bathrooms have been getting older, and at some point they will need to be replaced.
“And we’re winning more than our fair share in that market. We’re growing our volumes but certainly serving a more affordable project.”
More customers are switching to Wickes, and away from its up-market rivals, “because we offer a really high quality, affordable proposition,” Wood added.
Housing slowdown boosts Wickes
Wickes posted a £24.6m pre-tax profit in the six months to June, broadly flat year on year. The group hiked its dividend by 2.8 per cent to 3.7p per share.
Despite the slowdown facing the UK’s property market, Wood said the retailer is not reliant on home-movers for sales.
The retail boss pointed out that the group is “not exposed” to the new-build housing market, where housebuilders are cutting output targets, because these homes come with already-fitted kitchens and bathrooms.
Julie Palmer, managing director at real estate advisory BTG, said the slowdown in home-moving will help Wickes, as Brits opt to improve their existing homes rather than buying new ones.
“The slowing of the housing market across the year so far will also play into the demand for DIY and home improvements as people choose to stay put instead of moving while borrowing costs and stamp duty remain high, and uncertainty prevails,” she said.
Shares in Wickes jumped by 6.8 per cent in early trading to 188.6p.

items.title: Leading UK retailers ‘breaking law’ by not refunding customers for returned goods, Which? finds
items.summary: Consumer group says online shops routinely failed to reimburse delivery costs of unwanted purchases or cost of items Leading retailers are breaking the law by failing to properly refund customers for returned goods, a Which? investigation has found. Some of the UK’s biggest online shops routinely failed to reimburse delivery costs when customers returned unwanted purchases, while others failed to refund the cost of the goods themselves. Continue reading...
items.body:
Leading retailers are breaking the law by failing to properly refund customers for returned goods, a Which? investigation has found.
Some of the UK’s biggest online shops routinely failed to reimburse delivery costs when customers returned unwanted purchases, while others failed to refund the cost of the goods themselves.
The consumer champion, Which?, sent 12 mystery shoppers across Great Britain to buy more than 200 items from 17 big online retailers in June and July.
The shoppers then returned their purchases by post – the most common method of returning goods – and tracked the entire process, from the cost of returning an item to whether they received the correct refund.
John Lewis came out on top, with shoppers praising the retailer for keeping them informed at every stage of the returns process. Its strong performance has seen it become the first retailer to receive Which?’s new recommended provider for returns status.
But at the other end of the table was clothing and homeware retail chain Matalan, which failed to refund customers properly in a series of cases.
Matalan does not offer free returns, and refunded the cost of the returned product to just seven of Which?’s 12 mystery shoppers. None received a refund for their original delivery fee.
In one case, a shopper returned an item costing £3.99. They had initially paid £3 for delivery and a further £2.99 to return it. When no refund was received, they were left £9.98 out of pocket, despite being entitled to lose only the £2.99 return cost.
One mystery shopper said: “There’s a returns label in the bag but it’s so faded that I can’t read the instructions.”
Matalan has been approached for comment.
Reena Sewraz, retail editor at Which? , said: “Returning an online purchase shouldn’t be a battle to get your money back. Yet leading retailers are breaking the law by failing to give shoppers the refunds they are entitled to.”
 She said retailers “need to take responsibility for getting their returns processes right”, adding that shoppers “shouldn’t be left to foot the bill for retailers’ mistakes”.
Under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, online shoppers generally have the right to change their mind and cancel an order within 14 days of receiving it, with a further 14 days to return the goods. Retailers must normally refund the customer within 14 days of receiving the returned item, although some products – such as personalised goods and items with a hygiene seal – are exempt.
Retailers can make customers pay the cost of returning unwanted goods, but they must also refund the standard delivery charge originally paid. Customers are not entitled to a refund of any additional premium they paid for faster delivery.
River Island and Sports Direct failed to refund the original delivery fee in any of the cases tested by Which? – despite retailers being legally required to reimburse standard delivery charges when customers exercise their statutory right to cancel an online purchase.
A Sports Direct spokesperson said: “Unfortunately, we are not able to provide any meaningful comment on the ‘mystery shopper’ claims.
“Despite requesting the basic details of the orders from Which? to be able to understand what has or has not happened with the specific transactions, they have refused to supply the necessary information. We of course seek to address genuine customer concerns.”
River Island has been approached for comment.
Both retailers also charge customers to return unwanted goods. While retailers are allowed to do this, the combination of return charges and missing delivery refunds left Which?’s shoppers significantly out of pocket.
The investigation also uncovered failures to refund the cost of the goods themselves. Pets at Home refunded just six of Which?’s 12 mystery shoppers for products they had returned.
Pets at Home said: “We regularly review our policies and the information available on our website to ensure customers have access to clear and accessible guidance on our terms and conditions. As always, if customers have any questions or concerns, we would encourage them to contact us directly.”
The findings raise fresh questions about how effectively leading retailers are complying with consumer protection rules and leave customers at risk of losing money when they return unwanted online purchases.
Which? said some retailers such as M&S did not qualify in the mystery shop because it didn’t offer postal returns on items bought online under £10 if you checked out as a guest – instead, you have to return in-store.
Argos also did not offer postal returns, so similarly could not be included.

items.title: Pubs, hotels and gyms in Wales to get 30% business rates cut
items.summary: The cuts comes into effect in April, but the largest businesses will pay higher rates to fund the changes.
items.body:
Pubs, hotels and gyms in Wales to get 30% business rates cut
- Published
Taxes paid by pubs, hotels and cinemas in Wales will fall after the Welsh government announced a 30% cut in some business rates.
First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said hospitality, accommodation and leisure venues would receive the permanent cut in rates from April 2027.
"It is about helping businesses like this to thrive, so our communities can thrive," ap Iorwerth said on a visit to a pub in Cardiff.
The cut, which will be funded by an increase in the rates paid by businesses with the highest-value properties, was welcomed by UK Hospitality Cymru. But the trade body warned businesses still faced "massive amounts of taxation coming from all areas".
Business rates are collected by the Welsh government before being redistributed as direct funding to local authorities in Wales.
The government said the 30% cut would apply to small and medium-sized businesses with a rateable value below Â£51,000.
It will be funded by "a small increase" in the rates paid by the highest-value properties in Wales, that includes some hotels and firms with large sites such as supermarkets.
Ministers said this would ensure there was no reduction in the amount of funding for local authorities.
In July, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, also due to come into effect from April 2027.
Wales' first minister said the 30% cut delivered on his government's "promise to rebalance the way business rates work" in order to "bring more vibrancy into our high streets".
He said the change was about helping businesses "thrive", "so our communities can thrive, which is something I think people in all parts of Wales want to see".
"We've got to think, what can we do using the powers that we have? What are the most effective things that we can do with our toolkit in Welsh government?
"And this is something that we're able to do now, bringing this in from April next year, which is the earliest point realistically we can do this. This will make a difference."
The 30% rate cut will replace the current 15% temporary rate cut for hospitality businesses.
Finance Minister Elin Jones said this would be paid for by an increase in rates for the largest businesses to help nurture "thriving high streets" in Welsh communities.
Jones said it was right that the "burden will fall on the bigger businesses, not just in the hospitality sector" to pay higher rates, amounting to around 1p in every Â£1.
The minister's pint-pulling "could do with some work", according to Radyr Tap landlord Phil Newbould, though he said the rates cut would be "helpful" for the industry.
"I think there's more that can be done," Newbould added.
Across the two pubs he runs, Newbould said the cut was "not as huge as it sounds" and would amount to a saving of Â£3,000 a year.
He pointed to a UK-wide campaign to cut the rate of VAT paid by hospitality businesses, which is controlled by the UK government in Westminster, and which he said would cut costs significantly.
Cafe and wine bar, Kindred, has been open for five months in Cardiff city centre and owner Oliver Banks said it was "fantastic" to know that business rates would be cut.
"Hopefully it can mean that we have a little bit more wiggle room with what we do with our costs on food and drink, but it also means that it's a bit lighter on people, especially in the current climate of things," Banks said.
Hospitality was not a sector run by people with "oodles of money" and restaurant owners "aren't exactly running around in sports cars", he added.
Previous increases in costs, linked to inflation and the rise in the minimum wage, had seen prices inevitably rise for customers.
But Banks said "there's only so much you can do as a business owner, and you can't put that cost all on to the guests".
UK Hospitality Cymru director David Chapman said the costs facing the sector made running a business similar to "plate spinning when you're riding an exercise bike".
Chapman added: "You have massive amounts of taxation coming from all areas. We have a VAT problem besides business rates. We also have high inflation in the industry over the last few years. Energy costs have been high. Labour costs have gone up incredibly, really, with the National Insurance changes.
"And so it's been a very difficult job, a really difficult balancing act to keep going."
That being said, Chapman was keen to welcome the cut in business rates and said it was "the beginnings of a change which I hope will permanently enable our businesses to look at growth and to look at further employment, and to start to plan ahead".
The UK government, which is responsible for VAT and National Insurance, said the Chancellor prioritised support for the hospitality sector by cutting business rates by 20% for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England during his first week in office.
A spokesperson said: "As business rates are devolved, the business rates cut also means extra funding for the Welsh government, which can choose how to allocate it.
"Our Great British Summer Savings also benefited businesses and families from across the country, including Wales.
"The scheme increased footfall for businesses in these sectors over the summer, getting more people through the door and boosting local economies".

Redefining the omnichannel landscape: RTIH’s latest Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List
The latest edition of the RTIH Top 100 Retail Technology Influencers List is here! The list has seen a surge in popularity over the past few years, to the point that we’ve decided publishing it once a year is no longer enough. Here, then, is the second edition for 2026, with some names dropping out of the top 100 and some new names coming in (the latter are flagged as new entries for ease of reference).
Including the likes of retailers, brands, technologists, analysts, and consultants, the list celebrates individuals who are helping to redefine retail in a fast moving omnichannel age.
We use a variety of sources to select our top 100, including feedback from industry observers, research within our own networks, direct or third–party nominations via our website, and social media tools.
In addition to social presence, we also take into account award winners and judges, event speakers, books published, media appearances, and people building innovative companies, solutions etc in the retail space.
We hope you enjoy reading through the top 100 and, as always, if you would like to give feedback or believe that there are some glaring omissions, please feel free to get in touch.

items.body:
Primark changes its online mind as Popeyes UK gives back: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail systems deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Aldi UK, Skechers, Vue, Pentland Brands, Wakefern Food Corp., Hotel Chocolat, Morrisons, Never Fully Dressed, Best Buy, Rainbow, and Wendy's UK.
Aldi UK
Aldi UK reports completion of a SAP ERP system deployment across its store network. In a LinkedIn post, Nathan Loftus, National Supply Chain Director at Aldi UK, said: “And just like that.. The last 2.5 years working on transitioning Aldi UK across to the SAP ERP system is complete.”
He added: “From our first PO raised back in February 2024, to our final batch of Irish stores going live this week, it’s been a huge effort and a massive congratulations to all involved across the business.”
Responding to the post, Aldi UK’s Karolina Blaszczyk commented: “A huge milestone, congratulations to everyone involved! Having experienced the transition from an operational perspective, it’s clear how much work has gone into adapting processes while continuing to keep stock moving and stores supported. A massive collective effort across the business!”
Skechers
Skechers has selected KNAPP as technology partner for what is pitched as one of Europe’s largest fashion and footwear automated logistics projects, with a footprint of around 230,000 m² (2,475,699 sq ft) and a planned capacity of more than 3.3 million storage locations.
Opening in stages that will be complete by mid-2030, the logistics centre in Liège, Belgium will start to supply the European market from a single location at the close of 2028 and will be designed to allow future growth. The facility will handle up to ten million pairs of shoes per month.
An existing European distribution centre (EDC) in Milmort in the province of Liège is reaching its capacity limits. “For more than 23 years, Skechers has placed its trust in Wallonia as a strategic base for its European operations - and this new phase is the next chapter of our growth,” says David Weinberg, COO at Skechers. “This massive, automated and sustainable building puts us at the forefront of distribution to Europe and makes us fit for the future.”
DHL and Alibaba
DHL Group and Alibaba.com have inked a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to pursue the use of AI with a view to improving the end-to-end logistics experience for SMEs engaged in international trade. The pair intend to evaluate how AI powered tools can support customers throughout their international trade journey, from sourcing and supplier discovery to logistics quotation, booking and shipment execution to make cross-border trade simpler, faster and more accessible.
Katja Busch, Chief Commercial Officer DHL and Head of DHL Customer Solutions & Innovation, says: “SMEs are the backbone of the global economy, but many still face challenges navigating the complex rules, regulations, and trade requirements that come with international expansion. By bringing together Alibaba.com’s digital commerce expertise and DHL’s logistics capabilities, we want to explore how technology can help businesses spend less time managing complexity and more time focusing on growth.”
DHL and Alibaba.com will explore the integration of DHL Global Forwarding’s logistics services into Alibaba.com’s agentic AI platform Accio. Accio is a plug and play enterprise AI agent and agentic business team that equips businesses with an immediate, no-code taskforce designed to support the diverse operational needs of SMEs worldwide.
Accio will be able to connect to DHL Global Forwarding’s Quotation & Booking capabilities, enabling businesses to obtain real-time freight forwarding quotes, evaluate shipping options and book shipments more seamlessly. The new capability is the first in a planned suite of DHL logistics capabilities designed to automate key business tasks, improve operational efficiency and enable SMEs to scale more effectively.
Starbucks and Alipay
Starbucks and Ah Bao, Alipay’s AI agent, have launched a new AI powered service - the Coffee Alarm Clock - for Chinese consumers. Users can set this up by first opening the Alipay app, swiping right and telling Ah Bao “Buy me a Starbucks iced Americano at 10 a.m. every day”. They then create a personalised name for the alarm clock and enable Alipay notifications in the app settings. Then wait for Ah Bao to execute the task every day.
Ah Bao will ask follow-up questions to clarify the user’s needs if the request is incomplete or missing key information. The feature can also manage a wide range of recurring daily tasks, such as scheduling rides in advance. It will be made available to more merchants and brands.
Additionally, Ah Bao has introduced a new module at the top of its main page, allowing users to check and manage the status of their services.
Since its launch in June, Ah Bao has offered 10,000+ AI powered everyday services, spanning more than a dozen categories including hospitality, dining, travel and pet care. Users can tell Ah it what they need through natural conversations and complete various tasks, from paying utility bills and booking pet services to finding EV charging stations and hailing a self-driving car.
Brands including McDonald's, KFC, Mixue Bingcheng, Luckin Coffee and Haidilao have also integrated their services into Ah Bao, allowing consumers to place orders and make payments by chatting with the AI agent.
Primark
Primark has announced plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain, following the purchase of an automated fulfilment facility in Sheffield. A famous online laggard, the retailer launched a Click and Collect service in 2022, but owner Associated British Foods (ABF) now says there is "opportunity for profitable growth" through home deliveries.
The move, which was denied following media reports earlier this year, comes as Primark prepares to split from ABF. This is likely to complete in December 2027 and is expected to create two new FTSE 100 companies, with analysts predicting that Primark could be valued at as much as £9 billion, and the food part of the business £4 billion.
“This is a really big day for us here at Primark, with two significant announcements: Our decision to bring home delivery to Great Britain and expanding our franchise business. Exciting times ahead,” says Eoin Tonge, CEO at Primark.
A spokesperson for the retailer said: “Our stores will always be at the heart of Primark. But a lot has changed in online retail in recent years, from how customers shop and their expectations for online delivery. Combined with the digital progress we’ve made, and particularly the success of Click & Collect, we’re confident the time is right to give customers in Great Britain even more choice in how they shop with us.”
Jollyes Pets
UK retailer Jollyes Pets has chosen to work with Sona on a project involving 125+ stores, 1,000+ people, and one platform for AI driven scheduling, HR, recruitment, learning, payroll and communications.
“This is a big step for us in retail. Retail doesn't stand still. Footfall, seasonality, promotions all shift the picture week to week. Most operators treat that as a people problem. It's not. It's a data problem, and getting the right people in the right place at the right time is what keeps service consistent across 125+ stores,” says Steffen Wulff Petersen, Co-founder and CEO at Sona.
“A particular thank you to Adam Dury, CEO at Jollyes, for backing this from the top, and to Andrew Crooks, Head of Transformation, for driving this partnership forward.”
Vue
Vue has unveiled its transformed Vue Finchley Road location in London as the company invests in enhancing the big screen experience for customers. The refurbished venue features Lux and Ultra Lux seating, Laser by Barco projection technology, an expanded hot food offering and the arrival of Vue Your Way, making Finchley Road the first London venue to introduce this concept.
With Vue Your Way, people can download their tickets to their wallets to speed up the entrance process. They can scan their QR code at the ticket gates and head on through to build their own snack combos. They then pay at self-service checkouts, with staff members on hand if any issues occur, before heading into their screen to, hopefully, lose themselves in a good movie.
A spokesperson for Vue said: “This latest investment reflects our ongoing commitment to delivering the very best in big screen entertainment, combining industry leading technology with more personalised and flexible experiences for our customers. Thank you to our colleagues, partners and local community for supporting us throughout the refurbishment. We look forward to welcoming guests to experience the next chapter of Vue Finchley Road.”
The Golden Bear Group
StrongPoint reports that it is working with The Golden Bear Group, a UK specialist in outdoor retail. An AutoStore powered Pio solution will be installed at the company’s North Wales operation, comprising a Pio P200 system with 2,870 bins, five robots and two ConveyorPorts, with two additional ConveyorPort frames prepared for future expansion. Delivery is scheduled for Q3 2026.
“We are proud to have been selected as their first automation partner and are focused on delivering the best possible solution for their e-commerce needs. The UK is strategically important for StrongPoint, and we are seeing customers place increasing value on experience and delivery capability alongside solution design,” says James Palmer, VP Automation, Robotics & Professional Services at StrongPoint.
The Golden Bear Group is the home of Great Outdoor Depot, Jack Pyke Shop, Viper Tactical Shop and SPEERO Tackle Shop. The solution designed by StrongPoint will combine high density storage, intelligent software orchestration, and operational design expertise with the aim of delivering improved efficiency, scalability, and long-term performance for The Golden Bear Group’s e-commerce logistics operations.
Kramp Poland
Kramp Poland, a supplier of agricultural, forestry, and gardening products, has completed the implementation of LEAFIO Shelf Efficiency to streamline planogram creation and execution across its retail stores.
The retailer operates a network of over 160 PbK partner stores, each carrying a unique assortment of between 8,000 and 21,000 SKUs.
Across the network, there are up to 90,000 active SKUs. As this continued to grow, maintaining planograms through a fully manual process became increasingly difficult to scale.
Before the implementation, every new planogram was created manually. The merchandising team built a physical shelf at the head office, arranged products, photographed the finished layout, printed the planogram, and then distributed it to stores. This process created several operational challenges: creating and updating planograms required significant manual effort, new products could only be added once physical samples became available, and rolling out merchandising changes across stores was time-consuming.
With LEAFIO Shelf Efficiency, Kramp has transitioned to a centralised digital workflow where planograms can be created, updated, and shared with stores much more efficiently. Store employees access planograms through a mobile application, enabling more consistent execution while reducing manual work.
Patta
Streetwear brand Patta says it has reopened sales to the United States after deploying Reveni’s cross-border technology, allowing it to ship 4,000 parcels to American customers in a single product drop after tariffs had previously forced it to stop serving the market.
Patta, known for its limited edition product launches, had suspended US sales after customers were hit with unexpected import charges, leading many to refuse deliveries. It was left paying both export and reimport costs, making sales to one of its biggest international markets commercially unviable.
By implementing Reveni Atlas, it has been able to resume US sales while eliminating surprise duties for customers. The platform automatically calculates and manages tariff changes, allowing orders to be shipped with duties paid in advance and pass through customs without delays.
Tomas Overtoom, Business Growth at Patta, says: "You basically ship out a product, the customer just doesn't accept it because they get hit with tariffs. So you have to pay for the export but also reimporting it back again. It's extremely expensive. Ever since we have Atlas, we're extremely confident in using cross-border releases and implementing them, specifically for the US now."
Patta also replaced its previous returns platform with Reveni's integrated solution. The new platform connects directly with the brand's systems and third-party logistics provider, giving the team full visibility of every return while reducing manual administration. Patta also offers instant refunds to selected customers through the platform. During its latest product launch, it shipped 4,000 parcels to customers in the United States.
Never Fully Dressed
Persi reports go live with Never Fully Dressed. In a LinkedIn post, Liv Parkes, Founder and CEO at Persi, said: “When we first started speaking to the Never Fully Dressed team, one of the things that immediately clicked was how much they already think about styling. Not just: How do we sell this dress?. But: How do we show our customer all the ways she could wear it?"
She added: “That distinction is pretty much the reason Persi exists. Because I believe the biggest opportunity in fashion e-commerce isn't showing shoppers more products. It's helping them imagine more possibilities with the products they're already looking at. So, together we've launched: Style Bundler - multiple, completely shoppable ways to wear the item you're viewing; AI Stylist - personalised looks based on your style, occasion and what you're looking for (you can even upload and style something you already own.”
“Ultimately, we're solving a really simple customer question: "I like it. But how would I actually wear it?" Answer that at the point someone is deciding whether to buy and you make shopping easier for the customer and drive better commercial outcomes for the retailer. That's the win-win we've been working towards from day one. A huge thank you to the Never Fully Dressed team for trusting us with your customers and for being so brilliant to build with. And a very big moment for our small Persi team.”
Wakefern Food Corp.
Uber Technologies and Wakefern Food Corp. have announced that customers can now shop more than 375 Wakefern supermarket locations across the US Northeast through Uber Eats, with banners including ShopRite, Price Rite Marketplace, The Fresh Grocer, Morton Williams, Dearborn Market, Di Bruno Bros., Fairway Market, and Gourmet Garage.
“As a cooperative made up of family owned supermarkets with deep roots in communities across the Northeast, our focus has always been on serving our neighbours where and how they shop,” says Darren Caudill, Chief Sales Officer at Wakefern Food Corp. “Uber Eats gives our stores another way to serve customers where they are, making it easier to get the fresh foods, neighbourhood service and the value they count on with added speed and convenience.”
“Customers are increasingly looking for flexible ways to stock up on fresh groceries without compromising on selection or value,” says Prashant Garg, Head of North America, Uber Eats. “By partnering with Wakefern and adding more than 375 supermarkets to our platform, including beloved banners like ShopRite and Fairway Market, we’re continuing to build a marketplace that brings expansive choice, from full weekly grocery runs to last minute ingredients, into one seamless app experience.”
Landsec
Piccadilly Lights in Central London is introducing a reconfiguration of its famous 783.5 m curved screen. The new design will give brands extended periods for full screen domination, providing enhanced opportunities for global launches, theatrical style trailers and mixed reality, 3D DeepScreen special effects and more live interactivity with The Venue which sits underneath.
Landsec will maintain the patchwork formation on the digital display whilst introducing the flexibility to move between five or six brands. Long-term residents of Piccadilly Lights include Coca-Cola (since 1954), and Samsung (since 1994). Changes to the screen's format come into effect from January, ten years after Piccadilly Lights relaunched following a nine-month period of renovation which saw the installation of one curved LED screen.
In 2023, Landsec delivered The Venue, giving brands a physical stage in Piccadilly Circus. Events and experiences in The Venue can be live streamed to Piccadilly Lights. Brands that have leveraged both the locations together include L’Oreal, Fatal Fury, and HBO Max, which used both the screen and venue simultaneously to build awareness and engagement for its UK launch. A two-day immersive pop up delivered more than 9.5 million impressions, with 900 social posts and media coverage reaching 33 countries.
Hotel Chocolat
Hotel Chocolat has announced an exclusive partnership with Deliveroo, launching initially with five of its locations - Manchester Cross Street, Chiswick, Staines, St James's and Wimbledon. Customers will be able to shop the Velvetiser, Hotel Chocolat's new boxed selections, its signature selectors, and Velvetised Creams.
Carrie Martin, UK General Manager at Hotel Chocolat, says: “Thoughtful gifting has always been at the heart of what we do, and we're constantly looking at how we can make it easier for customers to mark the moments that matter.”
“Partnering with Deliveroo gives customers a completely new way to access and send Hotel Chocolat gifts: combining the quality and originality they expect from us with greater choice and flexibility. It’s an exciting next step in how we’re growing the brand and meeting customers where they want to shop.”
Suzy McClintock, VP Consumer at Deliveroo, says: “We are building a new destination for gifting at Deliveroo. Customers are no longer using our platform just to shop for themselves but to send something special to a loved one, whether for Valentine’s Day, Christmas, a birthday and more. As a true gifting specialist, Hotel Chocolat brings real brand authority and category expertise to our retail offer, and we are excited to help them reach more consumers who are on a mission to find a meaningful last minute gift.”
Stella McCartney
Stella McCartney has selected Proximity to support its clienteling strategy, with the latter’s app now live across 14 stores in the UK, Italy, France, Spain and the US. The brand was looking for a more connected way to support store teams and elevate the in-store experience.
By bringing customer insights, product information and day-to-day workflows together in a single app, Proximity gives associates the tools they need to deliver more personalised and informed service at every stage of the customer journey.
Pentland Brands
Inspectorio reports that Pentland Brands, owner of Speedo, Berghaus, Canterbury of New Zealand, Endura, ellesse, Red or Dead, KangaROOS and Mitre, is using its Responsible Sourcing & Compliance and Traceability & Transparency solutions.
“Operating responsibly has been part of Pentland Brands’ mission for decades, and we want to keep setting a standard in today’s competitive, global market,” says Richard Mason, Sustainability Director at Pentland Brands. “Inspectorio gives our teams and supplier partners the evidence to back our commitment to sustainability across every brand and tier of our supply chain, so responsibility is something we can demonstrate and improve, with flexibility to adapt in the future.”
“Inspectorio is strengthening how we approach both compliance and traceability across our supply chain,” says Abhy Thomas Joseph, COO at Pentland Brands. “The ability to track product journey data alongside our responsible sourcing programmes is going to give us a much clearer picture of where we stand, and where we need to improve.”
StockX
Klarna’s buy now pay later service is now available at checkout on StockX, a resale platform for products including sneakers, apparel, accessories, and trading cards. The launch expands a partnership already live across ten European markets and Australia into two of StockX’s largest markets, the US and Canada. The integration is powered by Adyen.
Shoppers will now have access to Klarna’s pay in 4 and longer term financing options.
"StockX has been a strong partner in Europe and Australia, and we're excited to bring that same experience to shoppers in the US and Canada,” said Lisa Robinson, Head of Partner Success, US East Coast and Canada at Klarna. “Resale is where a lot of the most engaged, digitally native consumers are shopping today, and giving them flexible ways to pay is exactly the kind of everyday value we want Klarna to deliver.”
“Delivering a best-in-class experience means unlocking access to the products our community is passionate about, whether they've been tracking something for months or discovered it five minutes ago,” says Peter Curran, Senior Vice President of Global Business Operations at StockX. “Expanding our partnership with Klarna into the US and Canada means more people can get what they're after, on payment terms that work for them.”
Best Buy
Checkout.com is supporting Best Buy with the next phase of the retailer’s Marketplace payments infrastructure. The Marketplace offering allows third-party sellers to integrate their products into BestBuy.com and its mobile app.
Checkout.com will provide card acquiring and debit routing capabilities. The tie up will support future payment methods, geographies and commerce models.
Antoine Nougué, Chief Revenue Officer at Checkout.com, says: “Best Buy has built a trusted experience to help customers navigate increasingly complex technology purchases. We’re proud to support the next phase of that evolution with modular technology, AI powered payment optimisation, and a hands-on approach to continued innovation and growth.”
Nature's Emporium
Nature's Emporium, a family owned Ontario organic and natural products grocer, has announced a new partnership with Retailgrid, an AI powered spreadsheet for retail. The aim here is to give Nature's Emporium's merchandising team a live, day-to-day view of the market and a repeatable process for acting on it.
Ahead of the partnership, Retailgrid's Price Radar platform monitored pricing across 2,500 retailers in the organic food category and modelled 20 million transactions across categories to analyse competitive positioning and identify opportunities to improve customer price perception and profitability. The same engine now powers Nature's Emporium's pricing programme.
Since it launched in late July, Retailgrid has completed daily data integration with Nature's Emporium's systems, started daily demand modelling and price elasticity analysis across the full assortment, and begun live price monitoring of four major natural products retailers and Amazon.ca.
Morrisons
Instaleap, a company providing software for e‑commerce fulfillment and last mile operations that was recently bought by Instacart, and Morrisons have announced a new partnership.
“We’re proud to partner with Morrisons, one of the UK’s most respected grocery retailers, as they continue to strengthen their omnichannel offering,” says Antonio Nunes, Head of Instaleap. "Consumers now increasingly expect ordering from their local supermarket to be as easy as ordering take-away. Meeting that demand at scale - efficiently, reliably - takes technology built specifically for grocery. That's exactly what we're giving Morrisons."
“We’re constantly looking for ways to make online grocery shopping easier and more convenient,” says Charlotte Exell, Group Online Director at Morrisons. “More of our customers are choosing to shop from us through one of our immediacy partners and they expect an efficient, dependable service every time. Working with Instaleap powers our online operations behind the scenes, helping us deliver fresh groceries directly to our customers’ doors quickly and reliably.”
Rainbow
Rainbow, a Chinese omnichannel retailer, has opened its upgraded Shahe sp@ce supermarket in Shenzhen. Developed in collaboration with Hanshow and Rainbow's technology subsidiary Lingzhi Digital Technology, the project marks its first Store Digital Twin
implementation, bringing together real-time store visibility, decision support and operational execution within a live retail environment.
Located in Shenzhen's Nanshan District, the Shahe sp@ce location has served the local community for nearly 17 years. In 2026, the wider Shahe Rainbow development was upgraded into an urban lifestyle destination that brings together retail, dining, services and entertainment. The move reflects Rainbow's broader ambition to expand the role of physical retail beyond transactions and create a more engaging destination for the surrounding community.
The newly opened sp@ce supermarket, built around Rainbow's "City • Garden • Food Hall" concept, features nine experiential areas designed around different food, lifestyle and community occasions. The store also incorporates Rainbow's intelligent fulfilment centre, supporting more efficient home delivery services and aiming to strengthen the connection between in-store shopping and its broader omnichannel retail model.
As its first Store Digital Twin enabled supermarket, the store brings together more than 17,000 IoT devices and AI capabilities to provide greater visibility into store conditions and support more timely operational decisions and actions.
Hanshow NexConnect Smart Cart, integrated with Lingzhi's proprietary AI shopping assistant, serves as a digital companion throughout the shopping journey, providing shoppers with access to product information, in-store navigation, promotional offers, and available checkout services.
At the shelf edge, Hanshow Nebular Ultra Electronic Shelf Labels support centimetre level product positioning, serving as a key component of the Store Digital Twin infrastructure. The tap to interact functionality extends the ESL from a price display medium into an interactive service touchpoint. Shoppers can access product details, traceability information, usage guidance and promotional content.
In shelf management scenarios, Hanshow combines electronic shelf labels, location intelligence, AI vision and robotics technologies to support out-of-shelf identification, merchandising management and shelf execution. Leveraging its proprietary Bailingniao retail AI model, Lingzhi Digital Technology contributes digital capabilities that support sales forecasting, replenishment strategies, task management and decision support.
Limited Space
Limited Space, an out-of-home (OOH) media owner, has announced the expansion of its portfolio with a new retail and leisure park network, following an exclusive digital media appointment across Legal & General’s UK property portfolio.
The initial roll-out introduces new digital media opportunities at prominent retail park locations spanning both England and Scotland, reaching over 21 million consumers annually.
Matt Gordon, Co-Founder and Director at Limited Space, says: "This expansion is a perfect fit for our business and a natural extension of what we already do so well. Retail and leisure parks complement our existing network brilliantly and allow us to offer extended reach to existing clients as well as bringing new brands into the OOH space.”
"We understand these audiences, how they move between destinations and the role each environment plays within the wider shopper journey. Bringing these locations into our portfolio creates exciting new opportunities for brands to reach consumers in highly relevant, high-intent moments, delivering greater flexibility, scale and impact across their media campaigns."
The installations represent the first phase of a wider roll-out in partnership with Legal & General, with the network set to continue expanding throughout 2026.
The Range
VoCoVo has announced a partnership with home, leisure and garden retailer The Range, that will see Series 5 (S5) Pro Headsets and Call Points rolled out across all 283 of its stores. This follows a one-store trial over the course of a year.
The Range colleagues will get instant, hands free communication through the headsets, replacing disruptive loudspeaker calls and reducing the need for them to search the shop floor for one another. The technology will help deliver faster, more responsive customer service by reducing waiting times at tills, service desks and across the shop floor.
Colleagues can contact managers and team members immediately for price and stock checks, quickly coordinate requests and assign tasks in real-time, while two-way Call Points will allow customers to request assistance at the touch of a button and connect with available colleagues.
A Store Manager at The Range says: “The headsets have made a hugely positive impact in-store for both colleagues and customers. Customer service has noticeably improved as queries are answered faster, stock checks are smoother and warehouse to shop floor communication is instant. This has already streamlined Deliveroo and Click & Collect, and I can see the headsets becoming invaluable during patio season. They’ve become essential to daily operations."
“The very impressive results already achieved in our store have laid the groundwork for much bigger savings across the store network. I can’t wait to see colleagues benefitting from the same technology.”
Beth Worrall, CEO at VoCoVo, says: “The initial trial with The Range has shown how they can achieve significant time and cost savings while maintaining outstanding service levels and the optimum in-store experience at the same time. We’re looking forward to working alongside the team to implement the technology across all its stores.”
DoorDash and SKIMS
DoorDash and SKIMS have announced a new partnership to offer on-demand delivery from all of the latter’s retail stores across the US. DoorDash is SKIMS’ first on-demand delivery partner, and SKIMS is the first brand on DoorDash to offer a selection spanning undergarments, everyday clothing, and outerwear.
"We were built on one idea: you should be able to get everything you need in your neighbourhood, right now. And increasingly, that's not just dinner, it's what you're wearing to dinner too,” says Shanna Prevé, Chief Revenue Officer at DoorDash. “SKIMS has built an iconic brand that’s become part of so many people’s everyday wardrobes, and that’s exactly what we want to your doorstep. We're proud to be SKIMS' first ever on-demand delivery partner, giving people a completely new way to shop a brand they already love."
SKIMS was co-founded in 2019 by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede.
“Our focus has always been on understanding what our customers need and finding better ways to serve them,” says Robert Norton, Chief Commercial Officer. “Our partnership with DoorDash gives customers greater flexibility and convenience when shopping SKIMS, making it easier to access the products they want, when they want them. It’s about putting the customer at the centre of the experience and providing a solution that works for them.’’
SKIMS is available on DoorDash from 17 stores across 11 states and Washington, D.C., with nine additional stores coming soon to the platform.
Wendy's UK
Wendy's UK has gone live with a new mobile app. In a LinkedIn post, Rob McGeown, Head of Technology EMEA, said: "I'm incredibly proud to see our new UK app officially launch this week for iOS.”
“When I joined Wendy's earlier this year, getting the app over the line was one of the biggest priorities in front of us. It's taken a huge amount of focus, collaboration and determination across our teams and partners to turn that ambition into something our customers can use."
He added: "And this is much more than just launching an app; It gives us a stronger digital foundation for how we engage with our customers, improve their experience and continue developing our digital proposition in the UK and Internationally. A massive thank you to everyone who has played a part in getting us here! I'm proud of what we have achieved and excited about what comes next."
Bing Lee and The Natural Grocery Company
SOLUM is expanding its electronic shelf label (ESL) business across Australia through new deployments with a consumer electronics retailer and grocery specialist. SOLUM is supporting the expansion of ESL deployments across multiple Bing Lee stores as part of the retailer's ongoing digital transformation initiatives.
In addition, it has supplied ESL solutions to The Natural Grocery Company, enabling real-time price updates, faster promotional changes, and improved pricing accuracy.
"Through our partnership with Bing Lee, we are proud to contribute to the retailer's store modernisation efforts," says Paul Kyriakos, General Manager at SOLUM Australia. "For The Natural Grocery Company, our ESL solution supports real-time pricing, rapid promotional updates, and greater pricing accuracy. A premium shopping experience is built not only on product quality, but also on a store environment that responds quickly and accurately to both retailer and customer needs."
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity is using AI to improve how donated goods are processed for sale online, helping to generate additional income.
The technology is being introduced across the charity’s retail network, which includes shops in Hereford, Gloucester, Market Drayton, Merry Hill, Ross-on-Wye, Shrewsbury, Stoke-on-Trent, Tipton, Wellington, West Bromwich and Worcester.
Provided by Minimist, the new AI powered system enables shop teams to create online listings across platforms such as eBay and Vinted by taking a single photograph of a donated item. In under 30 seconds, it can generate a complete listing, including a product description, pricing suggestion, size information and virtual model imagery where appropriate, giving donated goods access to a wider audience while helping retail teams process stock more efficiently.
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity does not receive any government funding and relies entirely on public contributions to operate its lifesaving service. Every sale made through its shops and online marketplaces helps fund its helicopters, fleet of critical care cars as well as the specialist crews and equipment required to deliver pre-hospital emergency care across its six country region.
Popeyes UK
Popeyes UK has announced the launch of Popeyes Rewards, its first ever loyalty programme. Built in-house by its technology team, this allows customers to earn points whether they order through the app, online, at the counter or via our self-service kiosks. Members earn points on every purchase, unlock exclusive rewards, and gain access to experiences inspired by the company's New Orleans heritage.
"For the first time, Popeyes Rewards gives back to our customers through Popeyes Points, and to kick things off, 2,000 points are waiting for you in the app, on us (only for the first six weeks, so hurry if you haven't claimed them yet!)," says James Clark, Head of Digital Marketing at Popeyes UK.
"We wanted this programme to feel unmistakably Popeyes, rather than just points and vouchers. To do that, we're bringing our New Orleans heritage to life, giving customers their very own Mardi Gras Moments throughout the year. First up: we're crowning one customer Popeyes' first ever "Lord of Mardi Gras" and sending them home with £10,000 and the ultimate Popeyes bragging rights. There's a lot more coming, and I'm excited to keep building it with this team. For now, go claim your points."

Nobody’s Child officially goes live with Persi AI powered styling and personalisation technology
Nobody's Child has deployed Persi technology in its e-commerce offering. In a LinkedIn post, Liv Parkes, Founder and CEO at Persi, said: “This is a retailer that was on my wish list before Persi was much more than an idea. So seeing our technology live on their website feels pretty surreal.”
She added: “When you're building something new, you're asking people to take a chance on more than just a product. You're asking them to believe in where it could go. And from our earliest conversations, Nobody’s Child did exactly that. They saw the opportunity for styling to become a much bigger part of the e-commerce experience, and trusted our small team to build it with them.”
Customers can now use Persi in two ways: PDP Style Bundle - multiple, completely shoppable ways to wear an item, whilst discovering complementary pieces complete the look; AI Stylist - personalised outfits based on their style, occasion and what they're looking for, including the ability to style something they already own.

CTO
In July, we reported that Shaun Perkinson had joined Gymshark as its new Chief Technology Officer. He took over from John Douglas who entered the world of retirement.
Ben Francis, CEO and Founder at Gymshark, commented: “Five years ago, John Douglas joined Gymshark to help us build the technology needed for our next stage of growth. Now, after an incredible career in technology, he's made the decision to retire. I can honestly say we wouldn't be where we are today without him.”
He added: “When John joined Gymshark, we were entering a pivotal stage in our journey. Over the last five years, he's led our technology function through some of the biggest moments in our growth. He's helped us scale, navigate complex challenges and set us up for the future, always bringing incredible experience, humility and calmness along the way. But what I'll remember most isn't what John built. It's the way he led. More than anything, John has made the people around him better. He's shared his experience generously, supported so many people across the business and left a lasting mark on our teams and our culture.”
Francis concluded: “John, thank you for everything you've done for Gymshark. Thank you for your leadership, your wisdom and the example you've set for all of us. I'm incredibly grateful for everything you've given this business and everyone in it. Wishing you nothing but happiness in this next chapter. You've more than earned it.”
Prior to Gymshark, Douglas was CTO at Tory Burch. His CV also includes stints at Burberry and MCM Fashion Group.

items.body:
Søstrene Grene stumps up DKK 380 million for automated logistics operation in Denmark and Netherlands
Danish retailer Søstrene Grene has invested DKK 380 million in an automated logistics setup in Denmark and the Netherlands, alongside an implementation of SAP technology.
In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: “Recently, we welcomed Danish business newspaper Børsen to our distribution centre in Aarslev for a closer look at how automation is helping us build for the future. Importantly, automation is not about replacing our employees. They are being trained to take on more specialised tasks, while automation primarily reduces our reliance on seasonal workers during peak periods and creates a safer working environment with less heavy lifting.”
It added: “The automated journey begins as soon as goods arrive at our distribution centre, where an inbound robotic solution receives and sorts them. In our e-commerce operation, mobile robots pick online orders before automated packing solutions prepare them for shipment. This not only makes our operation more efficient but also reduces the amount of packaging and empty space in each box.”
It concluded: “Automation is helping us increase efficiency, reduce CO₂ emissions across our logistics operations and create a better working environment for our employees - with fewer manual tasks and less heavy lifting. With this strong foundation, we are ready to pursue our ambition of reaching 500 stores across markets in the next few years.”
Digital receipts
Earlier this year, we reported that Søstrene Grene was rolling out ReceiptHero’s digital receipt technology across its network of stores.
The brand, known for its affordable home accessories and design led retail concept, has piloted the solution in Denmark, with a broader roll-out now in progress.
At the core of the initiative is ReceiptHero’s card linking technology, which allows shoppers to automatically receive digital receipts after paying in-store. Customers can connect their payment card and have receipts delivered instantly, removing the need for paper copies.
For those not using the retailer’s mobile app, people can access their receipt by tapping their phone on an NFC enabled terminal at checkout, opening the receipt directly in a mobile browser without requiring a download.
Through the new setup, Søstrene Grene can prompt customers to opt in to marketing communications or encourage app downloads at the Point of Sale. It says the initiative is designed to strengthen long-term customer relationships while also supporting more personalised in-store experiences when shoppers return.
